title: Organic Growth Lead
description:
Who we are 

Melotech is revolutionizing media and entertainment. We create art through technology for humans to enjoy. In just 24 months, our work has been heard, watched and loved for over 4 billion minutes worldwide.

Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR.

What you will do 

Melotech is scaling fast, and organic reach is one of the engines behind it. As Organic Growth Lead, you own that engine end to end: the creators, the formats, the trends and the numbers behind them. This is an organic growth role first, measured on how much reach every hour and every euro brings back. You work directly with our founders, our Growth Manager, product and data team.

Your first job is to turn organic reach into a machine: find the creators and communities that move culture, turn what works into repeatable playbooks, and run more experiments in a week than most teams run in a quarter.

On a typical day, your tasks may include:

- Creator network: finding and briefing creators at scale, from small accounts with loyal audiences to the ones that set trends, and keeping the ones that deliver

- Launches: getting our products in front of the communities where they can travel, at the right moment

- Trend spotting: catching formats and memes early and moving on them within days, not weeks

- Experiments: running many cheap tests every week, with clear rules for what wins and what gets killed, and turning the winners into playbooks the team can repeat

- New channels: finding places where attention is still cheap, from new communities to platforms nobody on the team is using yet

- Organic and paid together: working with our Growth Manager so organic winners get scaled with paid, and what paid learns feeds back into organic

- Measurement: knowing which number answers which question, for example what saves and shares tell you that views do not, and what each view really costs

- Tooling: building the trackers, scripts and automations you need, with platform data and AI tools as your daily coworkers

Who you are 

We're looking for a hands-on organic operator who lives on the platforms, or a creative growth generalist who has made things travel. Either way, you have done it yourself, not through a team or an agency, and you can show the numbers.

Typically, your profile will look like this:

- Interest: a strong interest in organic growth, creator marketing and social, ideally with hands-on experience from a startup, brand, app, creator agency or your own channels

- Breakouts you can show: you have made things go viral more than once, for a brand, an app or your own channels, and you can explain why it worked and what it cost

- Creator marketing at scale: you have run creator or UGC programs with many creators at once, negotiated the rates and written briefs that keep the content native; ideally you bring a network of creators, pages and managers

- Platform fluency: you know how TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts distribute content today, what makes a hook, and when a format is burning out

- Creativity with discipline: you come up with ideas nobody else would try, and then test them properly, with small budgets, kill rules and numbers

- Measurement: you track reach, engagement and cost per view in your own data, not in screenshots, and you judge every channel by what it brings back

- Data and tooling: you are fast in spreadsheets, ideally comfortable with SQL or Python, and you automate the boring parts with AI tools

- Pace: you thrive in a fast-paced and performance-oriented environment

- A big plus: you are or were a creator yourself, with a real following, and you're into media, entertainment, gaming or social

What makes this exciting 

You own a lever the whole company feels. Every breakout you engineer shows up directly in how fast we can grow, at a fraction of what paid reach would cost. You're not a cog in the machine but the captain of your own ship, rewarded for performance and respected for leadership. Flat hierarchies mean that your voice matters, your ideas get implemented, and your impact is immediate.

We pay competitive salaries and make you an owner of the business with equity. We work remotely to give you complete freedom over your life, while meeting regularly around the world for global offsites where we strategize, bond, and push boundaries together.

What the process will look like 

We hire on a rolling basis. Earliest starting date is always ASAP.

Once you begin our process, you can progress from start to offer within a week, depending on how quickly you can move through each stage:

- Initial interview: 30-minute introductory call, getting to know you

- Case interview: 90-minute case discussion, present and debate your skills

- Founder interview: 90-minute interview with our CEO, going deep on all topics

- Offer, contract signing and onboarding

Note: As we are still in stealth, you will learn more about Melotech as you progress through the stages. By the end of the Founder interview, you will have a full grasp of our business and the details of your role.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Revenue Systems
description:
Headquarters: New York City; Remote

Squarespace is seeking a talented Staff Software Engineer to support and evolve the systems at the core core of our monetization platform: billing, payments and orders. In this role, you will provide technical oversight over the critical monetization machinery that accepts orders, processes payments and bills subscriptions. You will regularly collaborate with engineering leadership and key product, strategy and finance stakeholders to align technical strategy with Squarespace’s business objectives. This is an opportunity to take on IC technical leadership responsibilities and own system architecture for high-visibility initiatives tied directly to Squarespace's core businesses.

This role is open to remote or hybrid working from our NYC office 3 days per week. You will report to the Director of Revenue Systems.

You'll Get To... 

- Own system architectural vision and design for critical areas of our business.

- Transform high-level system vision into estimated project plans for initiatives central to Squarespace’s strategy.

- Serve as technical lead and cross-functional liaison on business-critical projects, making and defending engineering decisions key to the success of the business.

- Mentor engineers on the team to deliver ever greater quality with ever growing autonomy.

- Drive best practices for engineering excellence and technical leadership, influence design reviews, question assumptions, point out pitfalls and foster shared understanding

- Set the engineering quality bar for the team through regular, high-quality code contributions across billing, orders and payments.

Who We're Looking For 

- 10 or more years experience specifying, delivering and maintaining complex distributed backend services.

- Significant experience with multiple programming languages (especially Java) and a broad range of tools like Springboot, hibernate, databases, etc.

- Demonstrated experience leading system architecture decisions across multiple teams or initiatives

- Proven ability to serve as a technical lead on cross-functional projects, aligning engineering and business goals without sacrificing engineering quality

- Experience working with billing, orders or payment systems at scale

Benefits & Perks 

- A choice between medical plans with an option for 100% covered premiums including medical, dental, and vision

- Supplemental Life and Disability Insurance plans

- Fertility and adoption benefits

- Headspace mindfulness app subscription

- Global Employee Assistance Program

- Retirement benefits with employer match

- Flexible paid time off

- 12 weeks paid parental leave and family care leave

- Pretax commuter benefit

- Education reimbursement

- Employee donation match to community organizations

- 7 Global Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)

- Dog-friendly workplace

- Free lunch and snacks

- Private rooftop

- Hack week twice per year

Cash Compensation Range: $170,000 - $299,000 USD

The base salary for this position will vary based on job-related criteria including relevant skills, experience, and location, among other factors.

In addition to the cash compensation above (which includes base salary and, where applicable for eligible roles, may include overtime pay), Squarespace employees are eligible to be granted an option to purchase our common stock. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive structure in addition to base salary.

About Squarespace 

Squarespace is a design-driven platform helping entrepreneurs build brands and businesses online. We empower millions of customers in more than 200 countries and territories with all the tools they need to create an online presence, build an audience, monetize, and scale their business. Our suite of products range from websites, domains, ecommerce, and marketing tools, as well as tools for scheduling with Acuity and creating and managing social media presence with Bio Sites and Unfold. Our team of more than 1,700 is headquartered in New York City, with offices in Dublin, Ireland, and Aveiro, Portugal. title: Energy Markets - France (CDD)
description:
About Us

At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, inverters and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel. Read more about what we’re building here .

France is one of the most important flexibility markets in Europe. This role is critical to accelerating Axle’s growth in France.

About the role

Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach in France.

At the core of our market expansion plans is market analysis. To maximise future revenue, we spend a lot of time understanding the value of flexibility in power markets around the world.

We are looking for a technical individual (data scientist, analyst or engineer) with strong knowledge of the French electricity markets and an instinct for commercial value.

You will become Axle’s internal expert on French power markets: understanding the market rules, modelling the value, and building relationships with system operators and regulators. We’re scrappy about method and rigorous about conclusions.

You will speak fluent French and English. Other European languages will also be an asset.

What you will be doing

- Developing a deep understanding of French energy markets and grid dynamics to understand how trading, compensation, penalties and cash flow work

- Jumping on the phone with grid operators, regulators and market stakeholders to validate hypotheses and make sense of data

- Building and optimising models of wholesale/NEBCO, capacity, balancing, ancillary services and local flexibility markets in France to forecast what different assets can earn

- Sizing the revenue opportunity across markets and products to shape where we expand next

- Building and evaluating different strategies for cycling a battery or load-shifting an EV charger

- Monitoring and shaping energy regulation to accelerate the growth of flexibility.

This is an opportunity to gain unique domain expertise and build the quantitative case for first-of-a-kind projects across the world.

What we think you need to be successful

- Deep quantitative and modelling ability (Python, SQL)

- Exceptional communication and the ability to turn data into actionable commercial insights

- Comfort moving fast and making decisions in an evolving environment

- Deep knowledge of French electricity markets (NEBCO, Mécanisme de Capacité, Mécanisme d’Ajustement, ancillary services…)

- Relationships with regulators, grid operators and other stakeholders (CRE, DGEC, RTE, Enedis, etc.) are a plus

What’s in it for you

This is a 12 month fixed-term contract (CDD). Compensation is highly competitive and dependent on experience.

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

You’ll be based in France. To maximise collaboration, we ask that you spend ~1 week per month working from our London office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse team, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

Interview process

- Initial interview

- Take-home exercise

- Final interview (in-person)

- Offer, references, and welcome to the team!

title: Software Engineer - Secure Container Images
description:
With more than 10 billion pulls , Canonical 's container images are trusted by developers worldwide to build and run software securely and at scale. That trust rests on our commitment to hardened, production-ready images.

We are advancing the state of the art with a new generation of Ubuntu-based container images we call "rocks": minimal images engineered for performance and usability and backed by long-term security commitments. As a member of the team, you will own the path from upstream source to published image, turning open source software into tested, signed, and continuously maintained artifacts that developers can deploy with confidence.

This is fast-paced, multi-disciplinary software engineering. Because most of the software we package originates from third-party upstreams, you will work across a broad range of container technologies and hundreds of open source projects, often in several programming languages, integrating and maintaining them so they are easy to consume on Ubuntu. Automation is central to the role: you will build the pipelines that package, build, test, and publish images at scale.

Your seniority in this role will reflect your software engineering experience and your ability to mentor and guide more junior colleagues.

Location: This role is based in the EMEA region 

This role entails


- Build and maintain a growing portfolio of high-quality, hardened container images

- Design and operate automated CI/CD pipelines that build, test, scan, sign, publish, promote, and retire images across environments and architectures

- Write tooling and tests to assess security compliance and cloud-native compatibility

- Work closely with the community and partners to share container expertise and keep our portfolio current with new features, patches, and applications

- Collaborate with our product security, platform, infrastructure, and customer-facing teams

- Contribute technical input to the team's decision-making

- Set the standard for quality, defining image standards that span security, compatibility, performance, size, and developer experience

- Grow our knowledge base and write about the work we do

- Work in a collaborative, agile, and globally distributed environment

- Mentor colleagues and contribute to hiring

- Work from home with global travel of up to 15% for internal and external events

What we are looking for in you


- Proficiency in Bash and Python

- Experience working with CI/CD systems (e.g. GitHub Actions, Jenkins)

- Experience building container images

- Command of at least one container management or orchestration tool (e.g. Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes)

- Hands-on experience with Linux systems, package management, build systems, release engineering, or artifact pipelines

- Clear communication and end-to-end ownership, spanning design, review, documentation, operation, and cross-team collaboration

- A commitment to sharing knowledge and helping those around you grow

- A genuine appetite for learning and for working outside your comfort zone

- A Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, a STEM field, or a similar discipline

- An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university

- Business level written and spoken English.

- Sincere personal motivation aligned with our mission.

- International travel 2-4 times a year for company events up to two weeks long.

- 0-7 years relevant experience.

In addition we expect that you will match our values, by being:


- Precise, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity.

- Reliable, delivering high quality work that builds trust and confidence.

- Accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable.

- Adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.

Nice-to-have skills


- A security-oriented maintenance mindset: you can investigate dependency and vulnerability findings, assess their impact, and deliver a safe fix

- An understanding of software supply chain security, with some experience generating and consuming artifacts such as SBOMs, signatures, provenance, or CVE reports

- Familiarity with GitOps principles and workflows

- Familiarity with additional languages such as Go or Rust

- Hands-on experience building minimal and distroless container images

- Knowledge of the OCI specifications

- Familiarity with security or compliance frameworks such as CIS, NIST, FedRAMP, or DISA STIG

- Evidence of contributions to open source projects

- A passion for embedding security across all stages of the engineering lifecycle (DevSecOps), and an interest in using AI or agentic development responsibly and safely

- Relevant Linux, container, or cloud-native certifications (such as CKS or DCA) are welcome

If your experience is close but does not match every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We value transferable experience from Linux packaging, release engineering, build systems, platform engineering, and open-source maintenance.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.


- Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person

- Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year

- Bi-annual compensation review

- Company recognition rewards

- 40 days annual leave per annum, including public holidays and our All Company holiday periods

- Maternity and paternity leave

- Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform

- Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues, with Priority Pass for lounge access

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. We are founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Powered by worldwide distributed collaboration since our inception in 2004, we believe tech and business leadership can emerge anywhere. We have no central headquarters. Most of us work from home, but we are exceptionally disciplined about this. We have very high expectations of all colleagues, and are champions of excellence. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration .

title: Distributed Systems Testing Software Engineer, Python / Go

title: Software Engineer, Computer Vision
description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

What you'll do

- Inspect boards. Improve automated optical inspection that finds missing, rotated and wrongly placed parts and bad solder, working alongside our AI agents.

- Pick reliably. Train and deploy the models that find parts in bins and trays, centre them on the nozzle and catch a clumped or dropped pick.

- Align precisely. Fiducial detection, calibration and image alignment for placements measured in fractions of a millimetre.

- Build the data loop. Decide what to capture, build labelling tools, and turn operator verdicts into training data.

- Go fast. Work with our high-speed cameras and GPU capture pipeline to move vision closer to real time.

- Measure it. Track accuracy in production, find where errors come from, and prove every change against past results.

What we look for

- You've shipped computer vision into production, beyond a notebook.

- Strong software engineering in Python, C++ or a comparable language.

- A mix of classical vision (geometry, calibration, template matching) and deep learning; you know when each is the right tool.

- Experience with industrial or machine-vision cameras is a bonus.

- You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

- You like the physical world: lighting, lenses and parts rotated by 90°.

Stack

- Vision: OpenCV, PyTorch and Lightning, ONNX Runtime on GPU, libtorch from Haskell

- Cameras: Basler GigE cameras via pylon, high-speed cameras with GPUDirect capture

- Services: Python and Haskell, PostgreSQL, Nix and NixOS

Pay

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

title: Data Steward (CoE Data & AI Governance)
description:
Offre d'Emploi : Data Steward (Center of Expertise Data & AI Governance - Central) 

Notre équipe Data & AI Governance recherche un·e Data Steward (f/m/d) en CDI basé·e à Lille / Paris .

Chez Decathlon, nous croyons au pouvoir du sport pour unir et inspirer. Notre mission : rendre le sport accessible au plus grand nombre, partout dans le monde. Pour y parvenir, la data est au cœur de notre stratégie, guidant chaque décision, de la conception du produit à l'expérience client. Notre défi ? La rendre gouvernée, sûre et exploitable. Tu rejoindras le Data & AI Governance Center of Expertise (CoE), une équipe dynamique de passionné·es, pour transformer notre patrimoine de données brutes en un actif certifié, auditable et actionnable, garantissant ainsi l’excellence de nos données et notre transition vers l'IA.

TA FUTURE CONTRIBUTION 

En tant que Data Steward , tu seras un référent clé en Gouvernance des données pour les membres de la communauté fédérée. Tu joueras un rôle pivot dans la définition, le déploiement et l’amélioration continue des standards de gouvernance, avec un focus sur les sujets de Data Knowledge et/ou Data Quality.

Ton temps sera partagé entre :

- L'accélération de la feuille de route centrale du CoE Data Governance : définition des standards stratégiques (Data Governance by Design, référencement des exigences de qualité métier, pilotage centralisé de la qualité des données, intégration des exigences de gouvernance dans le projet Data Contract de la Data Platform, et développement du Data Knowledge / Context Layer, etc.).

- L'accompagnement d'une Digital Unit / Domaine Métier (Supply Chain, Commerce, Digital Sports ou Corporate Operations) et d'équipes Pays : piloter la pratique de Data Stewardship, accompagner la montée en maturité, co-définir et piloter la trajectoire des OKR stratégiques (ex: 95% des données critiques respectant leur seuil de qualité) et animer la communauté.

TES RESPONSABILITÉS 

Tu vas pousser l'organisation vers l'excellence dans l'exécution de la gouvernance et de la qualité des données par tous les moyens nécessaires, notamment :

- Définir et faire évoluer le cadre de Data Governance :

- Unified Trust & DQ Metrics Store : Participer à la structuration du Data Quality Metrics Store pour offrir une vision unifiée et transparente de la santé des données.

- Gouvernance & Data Contracts : Collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe Data Platform pour veiller à ce que les exigences de gouvernance, de sécurité/conformité (classification, PII) et de qualité soient nativement intégrées dans le projet Data Contract ( "Define once, apply everywhere" ).

- Data Knowledge & Context Layer : Structurer la connaissance technico-fonctionnelle dans le catalogue de données (Collibra) et promouvoir la couche de contexte ( Context Layer ) pour faciliter la découvrabilité et le lignage des données.

- Shift-Left & Remédiation : Déployer le modèle de responsabilité partagée avec les producteurs de données ( Quality by Design ) et standardiser le suivi des plans de remédiation.

- Soutenir une Digital Unit / Domaine :

- Accompagner la pratique fonctionnelle et technique du Data Stewardship au sein d'une verticale dédiée.

- Réaliser des formations techniques et méthodologiques auprès des Data Stewards, Data Owners et producteurs.

- Évaluer la maturité Data Governance du domaine et accompagner les trajectoires vers la certification des actifs critiques.

- Apporter un support au quotidien et participer au recrutement des futurs coéquipiers.

- Contribuer à définir les standards d'excellence métier et évaluer le niveau d'expertise lors des recrutements de la filière Data Governance au sein des domaines.

CE QUE TU APPORTES 

- Leadership & Influence : Tu cultives des relations solides et basées sur la confiance avec un large éventail d'interlocuteurs internes et externes, en gérant de manière experte les attentes et en favorisant l'alignement sur les objectifs stratégiques. Tu fais preuve d'une forte capacité d'influence sans autorité directe, navigues efficacement dans les dynamiques organisationnelles et géres ta hiérarchie de manière proactive. Tu escalades les enjeux critiques de façon stratégique et en garantis la résolution.

- Rigueur & Analyse : Capacité à documenter, structurer des règles et résoudre des problèmes complexes

- Métier & Gouvernance : Les concepts de Data Governance, Data Quality Management, Data Lineage et Data Knowledge ne te sont pas inconnus

- Solide Compréhension Technique :

- Tu sais analyser, requêter et manipuler la donnée (langage SQL a minima).

- Tu comprends les grands principes d’architectures Data modernes (Data Lake, Data Products, Data Contracts,...).

- Tu as une connaissance des outils de Data Quality et de Data cataloging.

- Capacité d'articulation Tech & Business : Tu sais traduire des besoins métier complexes en exigences techniques de gouvernance et vice-versa.

STACK TECHNIQUE 

Dans ton quotidien, tu évolueras au sein d'un écosystème technologique moderne incluant :

- Gouvernance & Métadonnées : Collibra, Unity Catalog

- Data Architecture & Transformation : Databricks, DBT, Airflow, Python

QUALIFICATIONS 

- Diplôme (Licence, Master ou École d'Ingénieur) en Informatique, Data, Systèmes d'Information ou domaine connexe.

- 1-3 ans d'expérience au minimum en Data Governance, Data Stewardship, Data Quality ou gestion de programme data.

- Expérience probante dans l'animation de communautés et la conduite du changement.

- Anglais courant (niveau B2/C1 minimum) dans un environnement international.

CE QUE NOUS T’OFFRONS 

Organisation de travail hybride ;

Matériel fourni en accord avec tes missions et nos engagements sociétaux (Mac ou Windows) ;

Une équipe de projet locale au sein d'un réseau mondial (possibilité de carrière internationale) ;

Développement des compétences et accompagnement (diversité des projets, formations internes et externes, etc.) ;

Package de rémunération (actionnariat salarié, bonus mensuels/trimestriels).

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT EN FAVEUR DE L'INCLUSION ET DE L'ACCESSIBILITE 

Chez Decathlon, nous reconnaissons l'immense valeur qu'apporte la diversité à nos équipes et nous nous efforçons continuellement de favoriser et de cultiver un lieu de travail inclusif et équitable : c'est pourquoi l'Inclusion est l'un de nos Fondamentaux Humains. Nous encourageons les personnes de tous horizons et de toutes capacités à postuler, car nous sommes convaincu·es que la diversité des pensées, des cultures, des identités et des expériences vécues nous rend plus fort·es.

Decathlon s'engage également à offrir un processus de sélection inclusif et accessible à tous les candidat·es. En cas de besoin d'aménagement, tu peux en faire la demande via le formulaire de candidature, celle-ci sera confidentielle. Ces demandes n'affectent pas le résultat du processus de recrutement"

DECATHLON DIGITAL

title: Signal Processing & Data Engineer
description:
Who We Are

Limatica measures what batteries whisper. We turn the tiny voltage noise of battery cells into a quality verdict, far faster than conventional tests, and help cell manufacturers cut scrap.

We are a team of twelve in Chemnitz and Munich, spanning data, ML, HPC, hardware and industrialization. Early adopters across Europe and Asia already use our technology. In 2026 we move from pilots to production lines, and our data grows faster than our team.

What You'll Do

Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer.

- Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production
- Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour.
- Make throughput a design decision: Build modular, parameterizable nodes for our distributed processing pipeline and help bring them into our Rust-based production environment.
- Ship modules, not scripts: Automate evaluations end to end, from raw data to reports for our engineering team and our customers.
- Own customer projects technically: Assess requirements, communicate interim results and findings, and turn feedback into improvements.
What You Bring

- Measurement experience: A degree in electrical engineering (or comparable) and 3+ years with real-world measurement data. Sampling, noise, filtering and artifacts you know from practice, not just lectures.
- Physical intuition: You can explain why a feature makes sense, and you prefer a simple, well-understood method over a model nobody can explain.
- Data at scale: You think in throughput: data formats, intermediate results, distributed and cached processing.
- Clean engineering: Python, Git, tests and CI/CD as a matter of course. No Rust expertise needed, but the will to learn it.
- Customer confidence: Fluent German and English, written and spoken. You explain results clearly to engineers and managers alike.
Why Limatica

- Real ownership: Your own part of the pipeline and your first customer project within months. As we grow, this role can grow into technical lead.
- Learn what few get to learn: Electrochemistry, Rust in production and data engineering at scale, with real cells and international manufacturers.
- Share the upside: Salary package including virtual stock options.
- Invest in yourself: Additional holiday for personal learning
- Flexibility & wellbeing: Flexible hours, hybrid work, further benefits via Guud Card and free beverages
What it's like here: You get a lot of trust and a lot of room to shape things. We look for people who stay with a problem until it's solved and who enjoy the moments when a customer launch needs the whole team. Those are the moments where people here grow fastest. This role is intentionally a towards-senior position. You will take on increasing responsibility for pipeline modules and customer projects. Those who help shape the architecture and lead projects independently grow into a senior role with us.

title: Alliance & Delivery Manager, Pharma Partnerships
description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

We are looking for an Alliance & Delivery Manager to own Orakl's pharma partnerships after signature: the partner relationship, the delivery of each research program, and the growth of each account.

Orakl runs research programs for pharmaceutical companies on its virtual patient cohorts, combining compound screening, multi-omics and O-Predict analyses on the partner's assets. Several programs run in parallel on the same wet-lab and dry-lab teams, and the portfolio is growing. Delivery quality directly drives renewals and follow-on contracts.

This is a high-ownership, partner-facing role . You are the partner's main contact, you are accountable for delivery across our wet-lab and dry-lab teams, and you grow existing accounts. You will also scale our delivery processes and tooling: project tracking, capacity planning and partner reporting, automated wherever possible.

You will work closely with the Scientific Program & Operations Lead, Business Development, the Wet Lab, Data Science and Computational Biology leads, and Product. As the ideal candidate, you have already delivered complex scientific programs for pharma clients, and you are an expert at establishing partner trust.

What You'll Do

Own partner relationships: act as the main point of contact for each pharma partner from kick-off to final delivery. Map decision-makers, priorities and expectations for their asset, run the steering committees, attend key international conferences a few times per year and present results alongside our scientific teams.

Lead program delivery: translate each signed contract into an executable plan for the Wet Lab and Dry Lab teams, with owners, milestones and deliverables. Own the timeline, coordinate the experimental and computational work, and ensure every deliverable passes internal QC and review before it reaches the partner.

Manage capacity across programs: plan capacity with the Wet Lab and Dry Lab leads, arbitrate conflicts between programs and protect committed timelines. Centralise requests on delivery teams coming from partners and Business Development.

Manage risk and change: anticipate delivery risks, including results that change the plan, and escalate to the Scientific Program & Operations Lead with a recommendation. Agree and document scope and timeline changes with partners.

Scale delivery processes and tooling: scale our project management system in Asana, from program templates and timelines to portfolio and capacity views. Automate reporting and follow-up, deploy AI tools where they remove manual work, and document how we run programs.

Grow existing accounts: identify, qualify and convert follow-on opportunities within existing partnerships. Work with Business Development on scoping, proposals and pricing, and provide a feasibility assessment before anything is committed.

Plan scientific and BD materials: schedule conference and BD material cycles as part of the delivery plan, and coordinate partner approvals for any communication based on partnered programs.

Minimum Qualifications

- 4+ years in project management, alliance and/or account management, or partner delivery in biotech, pharma, a CRO or a techbio.

- Master's degree in a scientific or engineering field. A PhD is a strong plus.

- Demonstrated delivery of complex scientific programs: you have led multidisciplinary projects from plan to final deliverable, including when results reshaped the plan.

- Pharma-facing experience: you have managed pharma stakeholders through steering committees, negative results and scope negotiations.

- Commercial track record: you have identified and converted follow-on opportunities within existing accounts.

- Hands-on systems building: you have designed project management systems and automated recurring workflows.

- Working knowledge of oncology or molecular biology, sufficient to lead scientific discussions with our teams and partners.

- Fluent in English

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in precision oncology or at a pharma-facing CRO.

- Familiarity with patient-derived tumor models, omics or drug screening.

- Scripting (Python) or experience deploying automation and AI tools.

- Experience working with SOWs and contracts.

- Professional French.

Who You Are

- An owner: you take responsibility for outcomes across teams you do not manage, and you make explicit trade-offs when programs compete.

- Scientifically fluent: you understand what a result means for the partner's asset before you plan around it.

- Steady under pressure: you replan quickly if the data changes, and you deliver difficult news to partners clearly and early.

- A builder: you treat every recurring manual task as something to standardise or automate.

- Commercially minded: you recognise when a partner's needs extend beyond the signed scope and turn it into a proposal.

Why Join Orakl

- Own a portfolio of pharma partnerships. Represent Orakl from signature to final delivery, with direct access to partner decision-makers.

- Work on distinctive science. Deliver programs built on virtual patients cohorts, functional drug screening & multi-omics.

- Build the delivery model. Design how Orakl runs partnered programs as the portfolio scales.

- Work across disciplines every day. Alongside the biologists, data scientists and computational biologists who generate the results.

- Help shape the team. Define the delivery capabilities and future team needs as the partnership portfolio grows.

Interview Process

- Hiring Manager Call: align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

- Technical Deep Dive: discuss a pharma program you delivered: the plan, the problems, how you managed the partner and the outcome.

- Delivery Case: using an anonymised, representative scenario, build a plan, triage issues and prepare a steering committee. Present it to the team.

- Reference Call: speak with one or two people who have seen you manage partners and deliver programs.

- Founder Interview: discuss Orakl's partnership strategy and mutual ambitions.

What We Require

We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. title: Industrial Software Engineer - Railway Applications (m/w/d) 80-100%
description:
About Traila 

At Traila, we are dedicated to shaping the future of rail transport through cutting-edge technology. Since our founding in 2017, we have been driven by a passion for sustainability and excellence. We believe that rail transport is a cornerstone of a greener future, and our mission is to make it quieter, more efficient, and more reliable.

Our talented team is at the heart of this mission, and we are looking for an Industrial Software Engineer - Railway Applications to join us in developing robust software solutions that operate reliably in real-world railway environments.

What you will do 

- Industrial Software Development: Design, implement and maintain robust application software for industrial and railway products using C++, C#, Python or comparable technologies.

- Application & System Integration: Translate system and operational requirements into practical software functionality and integrate software with real hardware and physical systems.

- Hardware & Device Interfaces: Integrate sensors, actuators, controllers, DAQ systems and other industrial devices.

- Communication Protocols: Implement and troubleshoot interfaces such as CAN/CANopen, EtherCAT, TCP/IP and other industrial or vehicle communication protocols.

- Controls & Application Logic: Implement state machines, operational logic, control functionality and system behaviour required by the application.

- Commissioning & Field Support: Support installation, commissioning and field testing on prototypes, test systems and rail vehicles, including travel to customer and test sites when required.

- Diagnostics & Troubleshooting: Analyse logs, interfaces and system behaviour to identify root causes and solve software and integration issues efficiently.

- Testing & Validation: Develop unit, integration and system-level tests and contribute to HIL/SIL or other validation activities where relevant.

- Software Architecture, Quality & Controlled Releases: Own software architecture and release discipline, including configuration and version control, code reviews, test evidence and controlled software releases.

- Product Cybersecurity: Own threat assessment, secure access and software updates, vulnerability handling and lifecycle security maintenance; coordinate specialist security reviews and work with Systems/RAMS on vehicle interfaces and safety consequences.

- Technical Guidance & Mentoring: Review implementations, share practical software-engineering practices and mentor colleagues to strengthen consistency, maintainability and technical ownership across the team.

- Tools & Data: Develop tools for configuration, testing, diagnostics, data acquisition and analysis that support engineering and field activities.

- Documentation & Continuous Improvement: Maintain clear software and interface documentation and improve existing code as Traila products mature from development into deployed systems.

What you bring 

- Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical technical experience.

- Hands-on professional software-development experience in an industrial, automation, automotive, machinery or comparable technical environment.

- Proven professional railway software experience, including products released and maintained in service.

- Strong practical programming skills in C++, C#, Python or a comparable industrial software stack; you do not need to be an expert in every language listed.

- Experience developing software that interacts with real hardware, devices or physical systems.

- Experience taking software beyond prototypes into tested, maintainable and deployable industrial use.

- Practical railway software lifecycle experience aligned with EN 50716:2023, including requirements traceability, configuration management and verification/validation appropriate to the required software integrity level; relevant EN 50128 / EN 50657 predecessor experience is also valuable.

- Practical embedded or industrial cybersecurity experience, including secure credentials and access, signed software updates and rollback, and handling vulnerabilities in released products.

- Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills across software, communication and hardware interfaces.

- Experience with Git and structured software-development workflows.

- A practical ownership mindset: comfortable working directly with prototypes, test equipment and deployed systems and driving technical problems through to resolution.

- Ability to work effectively across engineering disciplines and communicate technical issues clearly.

Nice to have

- MATLAB/Simulink, HIL/SIL testing, data acquisition or condition-monitoring experience.

title: Workforce Intelligence & Analytics Manager
description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 

We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise. 

Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 

For more information, visit WPP.com. 

About WPP

WPP is the creative transformation company. Through One WPP and the Elevate28 transformation agenda, we are building a simpler, more integrated, agile and AI-powered enterprise. WPP’s Performance & Culture Center of Excellence brings together the capabilities that help our people, teams and organisation perform, grow and thrive. Within it, Enterprise Effectiveness aligns WPP’s organisation, workforce and teams around its strategic priorities and enables the change required to deliver them.

About the Role

The Workforce Intelligence & Analytics Manager is a contract role that will build the evidence base for the workforce and organisation decisions that matter most to WPP. This role will turn fragmented people, organisation and business data into clear insight, forward-looking scenarios and practical recommendations that help leaders decide where to invest, how to shape the workforce and how to organise for performance.

Reporting to the Global Head of Enterprise Effectiveness, you will support the wider Performance & Culture Center of Excellence while working closely with business, People & Culture, Finance, Data and Technology partners. You will establish a trusted workforce-intelligence capability that supports strategic workforce planning and informs priority organisation, workforce, team and people decisions across Enterprise Effectiveness and the wider Performance & Culture Center of Excellence. This is not a traditional reporting role. It combines strategic analytics, internal consulting and leadership of a four-person data and reporting team based in India. You will be expected to work through ambiguity, connect disparate data and systems, and progressively turn fragmented analytics into a more integrated, trusted and usable capability. As a contract appointment, the initial focus will be to establish the core workforce-intelligence approach, strengthen the India-based team and deliver insight against WPP’s highest-priority workforce and organisation questions.

Why This Role Matters

WPP’s transformation requires faster, better choices about work, skills, capacity, organisation and investment. Those choices cannot be made from disconnected dashboards or backward-looking metrics alone. In this role, you will create a more integrated view of the workforce, translate evidence into choices and trade-offs, and help leaders anticipate the implications of AI, changing client demand and new ways of working. The work will directly shape how WPP builds the capabilities, capacity and organisation required for Elevate28.

What You’ll Do

Build a trusted workforce intelligence capability

- Working with the Global Head of Enterprise Effectiveness, shape and build an enterprise workforce-intelligence approach that connects people, organisation and business data to the decisions leaders need to make.

- Define a focused set of workforce and organisational measures, dashboards and decision-support tools, moving reporting from activity and headcount toward capacity, capability, cost, productivity, risk and value.

- Partner with data owners and technology teams to map fragmented data and systems, define analytical requirements, and strengthen data definitions, quality, accessibility and responsible use, while being clear about limitations and the strength of the evidence.

- Establish repeatable analytical standards, governance and quality controls so insight is trusted, comparable and usable across WPP.

- Apply AI and automation to improve how workforce data is integrated, analysed and translated into decision support, while maintaining appropriate human judgement, transparency and responsible-use standards.

Enable strategic workforce planning

- Help business and People & Culture leaders translate strategy, growth priorities and choices about how work is organised into workforce demand, capability and capacity requirements.

- Build scenarios that show the implications of different choices, including developing, hiring, accessing external capability, automating, augmenting, redeploying and exiting work or roles.

- Assess the current workforce and future talent supply, including critical skills, capacity, cost, location and role mix, highlighting gaps, risks and investment priorities.

- Connect workforce planning to business and financial planning cycles so decisions are timely, owned and grounded in common assumptions.

Deliver forward-looking insight and decision support

- Use statistical analysis, forecasting and scenario modelling to identify emerging workforce and organisational risks, opportunities and patterns.

- Bring structure to ambiguous business questions, identify what can be answered with available data, test hypotheses and distinguish meaningful signals from correlation or noise.

- Turn analysis into clear choices, trade-offs and recommendations for senior leaders, including the consequences of action and inaction.

- Develop concise executive narratives and visualisations that make complex findings understandable without oversimplifying them.

Strengthen organisation and transformation decisions

- Provide analytical support for organisation design, organisational health, inclusion and impact, talent development, team effectiveness and change priorities across Performance and Culture.

- Create baselines and evaluate whether organisation and workforce interventions are improving the intended outcomes.

- Combine quantitative evidence with qualitative insight to explain not only what is happening, but why it matters and where targeted action is needed.

- Identify enterprise patterns across businesses, markets and functions and convert them into practical recommendations for leaders and Enterprise Effectiveness partners.

Scale tools, capability and adoption

- Build practical tools, templates and self-service products that improve the quality and consistency of workforce decisions.

- Coach People & Culture and business partners to interpret workforce insight, challenge assumptions and use scenarios in decision-making.

- Create a clear intake and prioritisation approach that focuses analytical capacity on the highest-value enterprise questions.

- Continuously improve the offer through user feedback, adoption evidence and emerging practice in workforce analytics, AI and organisational science.

- Lead and develop a four-person data and reporting team based in India, setting clear priorities, strengthening analytical and consulting capability, and shifting delivery from fragmented reporting toward higher-value workforce intelligence and decision support.

Minimum Qualifications

- Relevant experience applying data and analytics in finance, commercial, operational or other business settings, together with experience in people analytics, workforce intelligence or strategic workforce planning.

- Experience translating business questions into analytical approaches, workforce scenarios and decision-ready recommendations.

- Strong capability in data analysis, forecasting, modelling and visualisation, using appropriate business intelligence or analytical tools.

- Proven experience working through ambiguity and improving a fragmented data and analytics environment by connecting disparate sources and systems, strengthening definitions and quality, and establishing practical governance, privacy and ethical standards.

- Ability to communicate complex findings clearly and influence senior stakeholders in a complex organisation.

- AI fluency, including a practical understanding of how AI and automation can improve analytics, workforce planning and decision support, and how they may reshape work, skills, roles and workforce requirements.

- Experience leading and developing an analytics or reporting team, including setting priorities, assuring quality and building capability across locations.

- A degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Experience

- Experience applying financial, commercial or operational analysis to workforce investment, capacity, productivity or organisation decisions.

- Experience in a complex global, matrixed or multi-business organisation, ideally supporting enterprise transformation or significant workforce change.

- Proficiency with relevant business intelligence, data-visualisation or analytical tools, which may include Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python or R.

- Postgraduate study or relevant professional qualifications in analytics, finance, strategic workforce planning or a related field.

What Success Looks Like

- A clear enterprise workforce-intelligence proposition focused on the workforce and organisation decisions most critical to One WPP and Elevate28.

- A more integrated and trusted data foundation, with common definitions, practical governance and decision-support tools that connect workforce, organisation, business and financial insight.

- Workforce plans, scenarios and recommendations that materially improve decisions about skills, capacity, location, cost, AI and automation, technology and workforce shape.

- Stronger adoption of workforce insight by business and People & Culture leaders, with greater confidence in what the data can and cannot support.

- A focused, capable India-based team that delivers consistent reporting while building higher-value workforce intelligence and decision-support capability.

title: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.

This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.

As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: 

- Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.

- Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. 

- Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.

- Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.

- Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.

Success in this role looks like: 

- In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.

- By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.

- By 12 months , you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.

You should get in touch if: 

- Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes & investigative experience: You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care. You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.

- You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs: You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work. 

- Strong communication skills: You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

Bonus points if: 

- 

- You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide.

- You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance.

- You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan.

- You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC.

Benefits Overview :

- Financial Well-Being : Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.

- Physical Well-Being : We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

- Mental Well-Being : We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 

- Professional Development : Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks: 

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities

- Reimbursement for office setup expenses

- Monthly cell phone & internet stipend

- Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams

- Paid parental leave for all new parents

- And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. title: AI Engineer
description:
Who are we? 

Gain is the Private Markets Super App, a connected global platform transforming how leading investors, advisors, and corporates source, evaluate, and execute deals. By combining investment-grade intelligence, AI-powered workflows, and proprietary data in one unified platform, Gain enables top deal teams to move faster, reduce risk, and build conviction with confidence. 

Gain is trusted across more than $1 trillion of private capital, used by 100% of MBB and Big Four firms, and by 80% of the world’s top 20 M&A advisory houses. 

Recognized for fast innovation and impact, Gain has been named both US and EU Data Provider of the Year by PE Wire, awarded Global Financial Market Review’s Best Use of AI in Finance, and ranked in Sifted’s Top 100 Fastest-Growing Companies, the Forbes 1000, and the Deloitte Technology Fast 50. Gain operates globally with offices in New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Warsaw, and Bangalore. 

How we work 

- Predicting what isn't published. Many private companies publish little or no financial detail. Across a database of more than 5 million companies, we predict revenue and EBITDA from sparse labels, and we predict whether and when a company will be bought or sold, which is a time-to-event problem with censored data. 

- Agents on a messy web. Our agents search, navigate and extract company data points from sources that contradict each other, then decide which source to trust before committing to an answer. 

- Quality that holds while everything underneath moves. We're provider-agnostic. Model choices follow the evals, and we switch LLMs when the numbers say so. That only works if the evals are trusted. 

What will you do? 

The work is roughly half LLM agents and half custom ML, leaning slightly toward agents. 

- The design of our agent pipelines: architecture, tools, and which model for which task. You'll shape the technical direction with our AI Lead. 

- The evaluation behind agents and models: offline reference sets, live production evals, and the call on whether an improvement is real. 

- Our prediction models for financials and deals: features, validation, retraining, and knowing when a simpler model wins. 

- Getting work into production: trace where pipelines fail and fix the weakest links first, with compute, memory and model cost in view. 

- Raising the bar in the team through design reviews, pairing, and an eval-first habit that sticks. 

In your first six months you'll own the evals for our agent pipelines, propose where we invest next, and ship measurable improvements to both the agents and the prediction models. 

Who are you? 

- You've built and owned ML systems in production for years, typically 6+ in ML or software engineering. 

- In the last 1–2 years you've shipped LLM agents or pipelines that real users depend on, not demos. 

- You have modelling judgement. You've dealt with leakage, distribution shift and calibration on real data. 

- You measure before you claim. You can build an evaluation set and tell an honest improvement from a lucky one. 

- You care about the user outcome more than the technique. Ideas without a clear customer benefit don't get built here, however interesting. 

- Nice to have: time-to-event modelling, noisy or conflicting data sources, financial or private-company data. No finance background needed. 

The team 

You'll join our Data & AI team of six and report to Renan, our AI Lead who's been building production models for >10 years. Our engineering team runs the infrastructure, and you shape what runs on it. 

The stack 

- Core: Python (async, fully typed with Pydantic) and FastAPI 

- LLMs: multiple providers behind our own provider-agnostic layer, with Pydantic AI for typed agents. 

- Evals and observability: Pydantic Evals and Logfire 

- Data: PostgreSQL with pgvector 

- Cloud: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud Tasks), Docker, GitHub Actions 

What do we offer? 

- Competitive base salary and annual bonus linked to your performance / OKRs 

- Attractive benefits including health & wellbeing allowance, work-from-home budget, learning & coaching benefits, etc. 

- Flexible hybrid working model with 3 days per week in our Amsterdam office 

- Healthy work-life balance allowing for planability and personal commitments 

- Chance to grow with the company gaining increasing responsibilities, supported by lots of coaching and a feedback-driven approach 

- Tremendous learning and career progression opportunities 

- International environment with hubs in New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Warsaw, and Bangalore 

- Culture of trust, ownership and standard of excellence and a fun working atmosphere with regular outings and events 

- Post product-market fit and aspiring unicorn status - this is an excellent time to join & grow with us! 

Does this sound like a perfect match? 

We are proud of our wonderful product and believe it has lots of potential. We are growing fast and having fun while building our platform and company. Does this sound like a team you would like to become a part of? Click ‘Apply’ and submit your CV, we are excited to get to know you and show you what we do!

Your personal data will be processed for the purpose of conducting a recruitment process for the job position you apply for. If you provide Gain with explicit consent, your personal data will also be processed for the purpose of conducting future recruitment processes. description:
The Role 

We've grown to roughly 265 people working onsite from our Menlo Park headquarters, supported by a large network of remote U.S.-licensed clinicians â and part of the Series C is earmarked for acquisitions. The systems and the spaces holding all of that together were built for a much smaller company. We're hiring a Director of IT & Workplace to own them properly.

You'll own two halves of the same problem: the employee technology platform â identity, endpoints, networking, the SaaS portfolio, and our IT security posture â and the physical environment the company runs on, from space planning and physical security to the AV that customer demos and all-hands depend on. You'll inherit a small, capable team and be accountable for leveling it up. You'll be the named owner for IT controls in our HIPAA and SOC 2 programs, you'll own the IT and workplace budget, and when we acquire a company, you'll be the one integrating it.

Our Environment

- Treat protected health information and confidential data with the care our customers and their patients expect. This is non-negotiable in everything we do.

Workplace and facilities

- Manage physical security â access control and badging, visitor management, cameras, and emergency preparedness â aligned with our compliance obligations.

- Own conference room and event AV, including all-hands and customer visits, to a standard where the technology is never the story.
