Bei uns trägst du echte Verantwortung für die technische Grundlage, auf der alles aufbaut. Kein isoliertes Ticktabarbeiten – du gestaltest von Anfang an aktiv mit, wie unsere Systeme funktionieren und kommunizieren. 

- Freie Toolwahl 
Docker Desktop, Supabase, N8N, Hubspot-API, WordPress – du arbeitest mit dem Stack, der den Job erledigt. Und wenn du ein besseres Tool kennst, wollen wir davon hören.

- High-End Hardware nach Wahl 
Egal ob MacBook Pro oder Windows-Tower. Du bekommst die Maschine, auf der du am besten performst, inkl. 4K-Monitoren.

- Echter Einfluss auf die Architektur 
Du entscheidest mit, welche Technologien wir einsetzen, wie Schnittstellen aufgebaut sind und wie unser technisches Ökosystem langfristig aussieht.

- Kleine Teams statt Großraumbüro 
Du arbeitest in überschaubaren Teams, in denen man sich kennt und schnell ins Gespräch kommt.

- Musik bei der Arbeit 
Bei uns wird nicht mit der Stirn gerunzelt, wenn du dir Kopfhörer aufsetzt. Wenn es dir hilft (und keinen anderen stört), kannst du auch gerne Heavy Metal über eine Soundanlage an deinem Schreibtisch pumpen.

- Modernes Altbau-Büro im Herzen von Cottbus 
Hohe Decken, viel Tageslicht, Pflanzen in den Räumen und ein Innenhof für die Pause zwischendurch. Einen Einblick in unsere Räumlichkeiten kannst du dir auf unserer Website anschauen.

- Ergonomischer Arbeitsplatz mit moderner Ausstattung 
Rückenfreundlicher Stuhl, höhenverstellbarer Tisch, zwei große Monitore, ein hochwertiges Headset, ein leistungsstarker Laptop und eine ruhige Umgebung.

- Homeoffice-Möglichkeit 
Grundsätzlich arbeiten wir im Büro, weil Zusammenarbeit und Austausch vor Ort für uns wichtig sind. Gleichzeitig ist Home Office jederzeit möglich. Auch spontan und ohne lange Abstimmung.

- Vertrauensarbeitszeit ohne Kernzeiten 
Bei uns gibt es keine vorgeschriebenen Zeitfenster, in denen du anwesend sein musst.

- Flexible Teilzeitmodelle 
Ob 4-Tage-Woche, 30 Stunden oder ein individuelles Modell. Dein Job soll zu deinem Leben passen, nicht andersherum.

- Spontan Urlaub nehmen 
Manchmal braucht man einfach eine Auszeit. Wir planen unsere Teams so, dass auch spontane freie Tage möglich sind, ganz ohne Stress oder schlechtes Gewissen.

- Familienfreundliche Kultur 
Kranke Kinder, Elternabend oder kurzfristiger Arzttermin – wir wissen, dass solche Situationen zum Alltag gehören. Familie und Gesundheit haben bei uns Vorrang.

- Kurze Wege 
Bei uns musst du dich nicht durch die Hierarchien hangeln oder lange Mails schreiben, um gehört zu werden. Du kannst jederzeit direkt mit Kolleg:innen, Teamleads oder der Geschäftsführung sprechen. Entscheidungen fallen schnell, Austausch ist direkt und niemand sitzt „im Elfenbeinturm“.

- Mitgestalten statt nur abarbeiten 
Wir suchen Kolleg:innen, die mitdenken. Wenn du eine Idee hast, wie ein Prozess besser laufen kann, ein Tool sinnvoll wäre oder ein Workflow smarter funktionieren könnte, dann wirst du gehört.

- Sinnstiftende Arbeit 
Deine Tätigkeit hat direkten Einfluss auf das Leben von Menschen. Du unterstützt sie dabei, in Deutschland anzukommen, Sicherheit zu finden und ein neues Kapitel aufzuschlagen. Das ist keine trockene Büroarbeit – es ist Arbeit mit echter Bedeutung und spürbarer Wirkung.

- Feel-Good-Angebote im Haus 
Unsere Feel-Good-Managerin sorgt regelmäßig für kleine Auszeiten – von Nacken- und Schultermassagen über kurze Entspannungs- und Beauty-Sessions bis hin zu Momenten zum Durchatmen.

- Regelmäßige Team-Events 
Wir feiern gern. Sommerfest am See, gemütliche Weihnachtsfeier, Halloween-Sause, gemeinsame Lunches oder Afterwork-Dinner mit der Abteilung. Unsere Events sorgen dafür, dass wir als Team zusammenwachsen und den Arbeitsalltag auch mal beiseiteschieben können. Aber keine Sorge: Erscheinen ist keine Pflicht und eher Gehen auch kein Problem.

- Fitnessraum im Haus 
Unser eigener Fitnessraum steht dir direkt im Haus zur Verfügung – kostenlos, gut ausgestattet und jederzeit zugänglich.

Mögliche Aufgabenbereiche

Als Backend-Entwickler bei Migrando baust du die technischen Grundlagen, auf denen unser gesamtes Ökosystem läuft. Unsere Plattform besteht aus mehreren Portalen, Tools und Automatisierungen, die täglich von tausenden Nutzern verwendet werden.Du arbeitest eng mit Frontend, Design, SEO und Automatisierung zusammen und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Systeme stabil, sicher und performant laufen. Seien es saubere Logiken in Wordpress, Arbeit mit der Hubspot-API, Automatisierungen in N8N oder performante Datenbanken in Supabase – du entwickelst Lösungen, die langfristig funktionieren und skalieren können. 

- API-Integration & Schnittstellenbau 
Du bindest externe Dienste wie CRM-Systeme, Payment-Anbieter oder Marketing-Tools an, baust REST-Endpoints und sorgst für einen sicheren, zuverlässigen Datenaustausch.

- Entwicklung neuer Features 
Du baust serverseitige Logiken und neue Funktionen – von kleinen Plugins bis hin zu komplexen Modulen für unsere WordPress-Instanzen.

- Zusammenarbeit mit Frontend 
Du stimmst dich eng mit dem Frontend-Team ab, lieferst die passenden Endpunkte, unterstützt beim Deployment und denkst gemeinsam über technische Verbesserungen nach.

- Wordpress-Development 
Du programmierst individuelle Funktionen für Produktlogik, Checkout, Bestellprozesse oder Kundenbereiche.

- Datenbank-Management 
Du pflegst und optimierst Datenbanken, strukturierst Tabellen sinnvoll, verbesserst Queries und hältst unsere Datenstrukturen sauber und performant. Sei unsere Website-Datenbank oder eine Superbase-Datenbank mit internen Daten.

- Performance-Optimierung 
Du arbeitest an besseren Ladezeiten (Cloud- oder lokales Netzwerk), Query-Optimierungen, Caching-Strategien und einer insgesamt schnelleren Serverarchitektur.

- Automatisierung & Hintergrundprozesse 
Du entwickelst Cronjobs, automatisierte Datenverarbeitungen, N8N- oder Hubspot-Workflows und Hintergrundprozesse, die unsere täglichen Abläufe effizienter machen.

- Interne Tools weiterentwickeln 
Du arbeitest an kleinen Services, Modulen und Helferprozessen, die unsere Plattform und unser Team technisch voranbringen.

- Hubspot-Entwicklung 
Du beschäftigst dich mit Entwickler-Tools in Hubspot und kümmerst dich um eine reibungslose Anbindung in unser bestehendes Ökosystem.

- Evaluierung neuer Technologien 
Du hast Lust, neue Tools, Frameworks oder moderne WordPress-Architekturen (z. B. Headless-Ansätze) auszuprobieren und ins Team einzubringen.

Dein Profil

Bei uns zählen keine Abschlüsse oder Zertifikate – wichtig ist, dass du dein Handwerk beherrschst und praktische Erfahrungen in der Backend-Entwicklung gesammelt hast. Du weißt, wie man Schnittstellen baut, Datenbanken optimiert und Code schreibt, der nicht nur performt, sondern auch von anderen verstanden wird. Wenn du die Verantwortung nicht scheust und Lust hast, ein technisches Ökosystem aktiv mitzugestalten, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen. 

- Solide Erfahrung in der Backend-Entwicklung 
Du fühlst dich im Backend zuhause und entwickelst gerne Funktionen, die zuverlässig laufen, sauber strukturiert sind und sich gut erweitern lassen.

- PHP-Skills 
Du kennst dich mit moderner PHP-Entwicklung aus, fühlst dich mit OOP und grundlegenden Patterns wohl und weißt, wo heute steht.

- Umgang mit WordPress 
Du weißt, wie Themes und Plugins aufgebaut sind, arbeitest vielleicht sogar mit Hooks und fühlst dich im WP-Ökosystem zu Hause.

- Sicherer Umgang mit Datenbanken 
Du kannst Datenbankstrukturen sinnvoll planen und nutzen. Du kennst Best-Practices und fühlst dich im Umgang mit Datenbanken wohl.

- Sauberer, gut strukturierter Code 
Lesbarkeit und Architektur sind für dich keine Nice-to-haves. Du schreibst Code, den andere in sechs Monaten noch verstehen – inklusive dir selbst.

- Erfahrungen im API-Bereich 
Du hast schon mit REST- oder vergleichbaren Schnittstellen gearbeitet und weißt, wie man Services integriert, autorisiert und möglicherweise auch eigene Endpunkte erstellt.

- Sicherheitsfokus 
Du kennst typische Schwachstellen und weißt, wie man sich dagegen absichert (In unserem Fall: Webseite-Schwachstellen - unsere internen Tools sind nur innerhalb des Netzwerks verfügbar).

- Datenschutz-Verständnis 
Wir arbeiten mit sensiblen Kundendaten. Wir erwarten ein Bewusstsein für sichere Speicherung und Verarbeitung dieser Daten.

- Offenheit für Neues 
Du hast Lust, dich in neue Tools oder Frameworks einzuarbeiten und dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln.

- Verantwortungsbewusstsein 
Du denkst bei deiner Arbeit auch an Skalierbarkeit, Datenintegrität und langfristige Wartbarkeit. “Quick and dirty” darf auch mal sein - aber das möchte abgesprochen werden.

- Einfache Kommunikation 
Du bist kommunikativ und offen. Eigentlich wollen wir hier keine generischen Sachen schreiben, aber dieser Punkt ist wichtig. Gute Zusammenarbeit ist uns ebenso wichtig wie reines Know-how. Ein Kollege, mit dem die Zusammenarbeit angenehm und reibungslos ist, kann im Alltag wertvoller sein als jemand mit mehr Erfahrung, mit dem die Kommunikation aber eher schleppend ist.

- Deutsch oder Englisch 
Du sprichst Deutsch oder Englisch oder am besten beides (ca. B2-Level). Keine Sorge, wir erwarten keinen Nachweis des Sprachniveaus.

title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer (Wiesbaden, Germany) - Relocation Provided
description:
Consequential Work. Dedicated People. 

About Onebrief 

Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

About the Role 

We are hiring a Site Reliability Engineer to support Onebrief deployments across on-premises hardware, virtualized systems, and cloud environments.

This is a hands-on infrastructure role focused on Linux administration, hardware maintenance, and application reliability. You will manage Linux servers, NVIDIA DGX Spark or similar AI computing systems, rack-mounted equipment, and the applications running on them. You will also support workloads deployed on virtual machines, Kubernetes, and cloud infrastructure.

Your primary responsibility is keeping these environments operational and maintaining a 99.5% application availability target . You will troubleshoot production issues, perform routine maintenance, and work with engineering teams to improve system reliability.

You will work primarily on-site with military customers in Wiesbaden, Germany, alongside Onebrief Outcome Engineers, Mission Success, GRC, and Infrastructure teams. Some environments have limited connectivity or operate on air-gapped networks, requiring practical troubleshooting skills and careful planning for maintenance and deployments.

Security Clearance, Location, and Onsite Requirements 

This role requires regular on-site work at customer locations in and around Wiesbaden, Germany. Relocation assistance is available.

An active Top Secret clearance is required, with the ability to obtain SCI eligibility. Active Security+ (or another DoD 8570.01-approved credential) is required, or the ability to obtain one within 30 days of hire.

About You 

You have a strong background in Linux systems administration and experience supporting production applications. You are comfortable working directly with server hardware, troubleshooting operating system issues, and diagnosing application failures. You understand how infrastructure problems affect the software running on it and know how to narrow down the cause of an outage.

You take responsibility for the systems you maintain and communicate clearly when problems arise. You can work independently at a customer site while collaborating with remote engineering teams. You value good documentation, practical automation, and fixing recurring problems.

What You'll Do 

- Maintain Linux systems and hardware: Install, configure, patch, and troubleshoot Linux servers, NVIDIA DGX Spark or similar GPU systems, rack-mounted equipment, and virtual machines. Handle hardware diagnostics, firmware updates, and routine maintenance.

- Operate production applications: Deploy, monitor, upgrade, and troubleshoot applications running on Linux, virtual machines, Kubernetes, and cloud infrastructure. Work with software engineers to resolve application issues and improve deployment processes.

- Maintain application availability: Work toward a 99.5% uptime target across assigned environments. Monitor application and system health, respond to alerts, investigate performance issues, and address problems before they cause extended outages.

- Respond to incidents: Diagnose hardware, operating system, network, and application failures. Restore service, coordinate escalations, and document root causes and corrective actions through After Action Reviews (AARs).

- Improve operations through automation: Use scripting and configuration management tools to simplify deployments, patching, monitoring, and recovery. Support secure operations in cloud, on-premises, and air-gapped environments.

What We Look For 

- Active Top Secret clearance, with the ability to obtain SCI eligibility.

- 5+ years of experience in Linux systems administration, SRE, infrastructure engineering, or a related role.

- Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills, including networking, storage, system performance, and security configuration.

- Hands-on experience maintaining physical servers and troubleshooting hardware failures.

- Experience supporting production applications on Linux servers, virtual machines, or containers.

- Familiarity with Docker and Kubernetes, including application deployments and basic troubleshooting.

- Understanding of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, and firewalls.

- Experience with monitoring, incident response, and root cause analysis.

- Ability to automate routine administration tasks using Bash or Python.

Nice to have qualifications 

- Working knowledge of at least one cloud platform, preferably AWS or Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).

- Experience with NVIDIA DGX Spark, GPU servers, or similar AI computing hardware.

- Experience with virtualization platforms such as VMware, Proxmox, or Nutanix.

- Familiarity with infrastructure automation tools such as Terraform or Ansible.

- Experience with Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, or similar monitoring tools.

- Experience supporting systems in DoD, classified, or air-gapped environments.

- Familiarity with DoD security requirements, including STIGs and RMF.

- Experience with CI/CD pipelines, GitOps, or Kubernetes administration.

- Relevant certifications such as RHCSA, RHCE, CKA, or AWS certifications.

Notice to Third Party Recruitment Agencies 
Please note that Onebrief does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of an executed Recruitment Services Agreement, there will be no obligation to any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without an agreement Onebrief explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, shall be deemed the property of Onebrief.

title: Global Investigator (Triage)
description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

As a Global Investigator on the triage team, you will be the first line of operational defense in a fast-moving crypto disruption pipeline. You will process inbound complaint data, validate outputs from our artificial-intelligence (AI) investigation platform, and route cases into the investigative pipelines that result in frozen scam proceeds and seized assets. You will hold the disposition pen: your call is what turns a complaint into a freeze, a takedown, a recovery handoff, a legal-process draft, a victim notification, or a close.

The impact you will have: 

- Validate and route hundreds of complaint dispositions per week, feeding a live asset-recovery pipeline.

- Catch the AI errors that matter, such as false positives, merged syndicates, and misclassified scam patterns, before they propagate downstream.

- Enrich complaint selectors using a stack of more than forty commercial data-source integrations.

- Own clean shift handoffs so the around-the-clock operation never drops a lead, providing EMEA-hours coverage that keeps the queue moving while colleagues in other regions are offline.

What we’re looking for: 

- Investigative or analytical experience in the private or public sector. One to three years is fine: we want hungry people who want to grow into deep crypto expertise.

- Strong AI fluency, meaning comfort using AI tools as a daily co-pilot, plus the judgment to know when they are wrong.

- Excitement to deepen blockchain analysis skills.

- Comfort operating in a fast-paced, fluid environment where the project's scope and emphasis may shift quarter to quarter.

- Strong written and verbal communication.

About the Team: 

- The team is built around a mix of seasoned investigators and rising talent. Triage investigators sit alongside experienced crypto tracers and intelligence-trained individual contributors, and the seat is designed to accelerate your development.

Team Operating Rhythms: 

- Daily schedule: standard business hours in your local time zone.

- Collaboration: coordinate with global teammates for handoffs on time-sensitive items, giving the wider operation near follow-the-sun coverage.

On-Call Responsibilities: 

- Formal on-call rotation for high-priority events, such as hacks, law-enforcement support, and other time-sensitive matters.

- Weekly rotation, with occasional weekend coverage as needed.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position: 

- React quickly to incoming complaint surges and live takedown events.

- Continuously learn new patterns in crypto-enabled crime.

Application Instructions 

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM 

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

- Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

- Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

- First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

- Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

- References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

- Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

- Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM 

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

- Accelerate repeatable workflows

- Structure and solve problems

- Improve output quality

- Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM 

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

- Priorities and targets to change quickly

- Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

- A high level of personal ownership and accountability

- Close collaboration across teams and functions

- Frequent, high-touch communication

- Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

- A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 

Leadership Principles 

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

- Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

- Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

- Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission 

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. 

Privacy Policy and Additional Information 

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy .

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates. 

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form .

Recruitment agencies 

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

title: Senior Quality Engineer - Tellent Intelligence (AI)
description:
Note: The listed salary range is based on the salary range for the Netherlands. Salary ranges may vary by location. 

About the Role 

As a Senior Quality Engineer – Tellent Intelligence (AI) , you'll own and grow the quality of the AI-powered experiences built by our Tellent Intelligence team alongside our existing QE team. You'll help shape how we test applications powered by large language models (LLMs) and AI agents, ensuring they are reliable, safe, and deliver high-quality experiences for our customers.

You'll expand our end-to-end test coverage in Playwright and help build robust approaches for validating AI-powered systems, where quality extends beyond functional correctness. This is a hands-on, collaborative role with genuine ownership, direct impact on product development, and the opportunity to shape how we test AI at Tellent.

Your 12-Month Journey 

- During your first 3 months: You'll get to know our Tellent Intelligence domain, engineering practices, AI-powered features, and quality standards. You'll learn our testing framework and development workflow while contributing to automated, exploratory, and AI-focused testing.

- Within 6 months: You'll take ownership of quality across key AI-powered features, expand our Playwright test coverage, and work closely with engineers to validate AI behaviour, prompts, and model-driven functionality throughout development.

- After 1 year: You'll be a trusted quality partner within the Tellent Intelligence team, driving improvements to our AI testing strategy, strengthening our automation framework, and helping shape how we build reliable, safe, and responsible AI experiences across Tellent.

What You'll Be Doing 

- Work closely with fellow Quality Engineers to bring our test automation strategy to life across the Tellent Intelligence domain, taking shared ownership and continuously improving it as our platform evolves.

- Partner with developers, AI engineers, and fellow QEs to embed quality early in the development process, sharing knowledge and shaping testing practices collaboratively.

- Design and execute comprehensive test plans, test cases, and automated test suites across frontend, backend, and AI-powered functionality.

- Develop into a product domain expert, using your understanding to identify risks early and guide quality decisions across the Tellent Intelligence domain.

- Design and execute testing strategies for AI-powered features, validating not only functional correctness but also the quality, relevance, consistency, and safety of AI-generated outputs.

- Develop approaches for testing non-deterministic systems by creating evaluation datasets, defining quality benchmarks, and identifying hallucinations, bias, regressions, and prompt-related issues as models and prompts evolve.

- Partner with engineers to validate prompt changes, AI agent behaviour, and safety guardrails, ensuring our AI behaves reliably and responsibly before reaching customers.

- Continuously improve how we evaluate AI quality by helping establish best practices, quality metrics, and testing frameworks for LLM-powered applications.

What You Bring 

- Strong QA experience: Several years of hands-on quality engineering, with senior-level ownership of testing for complex web applications.

- AI quality mindset: Experience testing AI-powered applications, LLM-based products, conversational AI, or machine learning systems is a strong plus. If you haven't worked directly with AI before, you're excited to learn and apply quality engineering principles to this rapidly evolving space.

- E2E automation: Experience building and maintaining end-to-end test suites in Playwright.

- API & backend testing skills: Experience testing APIs and backend services.

title: Director of Engineering, Frontend technologies, Marketplace Technologies
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

About the Role 

We are looking for a Director of Engineering to lead the Frontend Technologies domain within Marketplace. In this role, your mission will be two-fold: 

- Pivot our frontend setup for bigger efficiency : we have been operating in mostly the same frontend setup for at least 6 years, and recognize that change is imminent.

- Drive strategic engineering initiatives : architect and implement platform-specific changes that enhance modularity, autonomy, resilience, and performance across Android, iOS, and Web. 

You will have to balance and prioritize foundational capabilities - such as Design Systems, CI/CD, Modularization, App Releases, Performance, and Global UI quality - to optimize both frontend developer velocity and user satisfaction.

You will lead 4 Engineering Managers and 3 Staff Engineers and set and implement the FE strategy, which will impact the roadmaps of 9 Product domains within the Marketplace.

In this position, you will 

Strategically: 

- Ensure the most effective frontend setup for the Marketplace. We have 40+ teams, each with 3 frontend engineers (iOS, Android, and Web) in the Marketplace unit. We know this will look different in two years. Deciding what different means, and getting 9 product domains to fund it, is the job

- Drive Technology Strategy: Set and drive the future technology strategy for frontends, establishing a modular, scalable architecture that enables rapid development and strategic growth. Basically - raise the technological bar for all Marketplace unit. 

- Refine the domain's identity: Take sole ownership of shaping its future, successfully integrating Design Systems and engineering to treat our frontend platforms as a cohesive product.

Tactically : 

- Lead frontends: Lead a horizontal, platform-focused domain containing Android, iOS, Web, and Design System teams.

- Lead Initiatives: Oversee Marketplace-wide technical tooling, core libraries, and frameworks. Lead strategic projects, i.e., frontend modularization and modernization (SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose), native automated testing.

- Elevate global UI quality: Integrate design systems and accessibility into the frontend ecosystem to consolidate technical, visual and interaction quality standards. Support UI experimentation.

- Ensure Resilience & Reliability: Maintain robust release processes, Marketplace frontend quality, and performance monitoring to reduce downtime and ensure a consistent member experience.

- Innovate & Optimize: Drive AI-efficiency enablement in frontend development and explore cross-platform frontend development opportunities to increase engineering speed and productivity.

A lot of this work will be influencing without formal authority : Champion the frontend technical vision among your director peers, influencing the leaders of 9 Product domains to accommodate and prioritize platform-wide changes across 40+ teams.

About you 

How much of a technical acumen? Enough to have in depth conversations with our direct reports. You will have 4 strong technical EMs reporting to you, as well as 3 world-class staff engineers. We don’t think you need to match their technical competencies (that’s a stretch!), but you have to be able to speak their language, understand problems at their essence, and be able to consolidate and multiply their inputs, including being able to disagree objectively.

Leadership: you have a track record of making level change in the organizations that you lead (rather than 20% change). Consolidating your team views and making coherent strategy out of those views is step one. Step two is even more important: being able to implement these changes in your domain, and more so - across other domains in the marketplace - is a foundational ability you carry. In practice, that means you have at least 2 years of experience leading leaders and 5 years of experience influencing without authority. 

Change horizon: You are comfortable holding two timeframes at once. We need someone who can say, "Here is what our frontend setup should look like in two years, and here is why" AND name the clear deliverable that has to ship in the first quarter to make that end state reachable. Leaders who only do the second are common. Leaders who only do the first are entertaining. We need both.

What this role is not: This is not a hands-on frontend or release-engineering role. You will not be tuning CI, owning the release train, or reviewing architecture decisions yourself — you’ll have 4 strong EMs and 3 Staff Engineers close to the details, and your job is to turn their technical judgment into direction, alignment, and organizational change. If your strongest work is deep in the mechanics, you'll be underused here. If your strongest work is changing how 40+ teams operate, you'll be busy.

Work perks 

- The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Digital mental and emotional health support and Employee Assistant Program (EAP)

- Frequent team-building events

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- A daily lunch allowance

- ClassPass (Gym Membership subsidy)

- Pension plan with total contribution of 12%, 8% by the Company and 4% by employee

- A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted

- An NS mobility card

- The opportunity to spend up to 90 days per year - 21 of which can be spent working outside of the EU - on workation

- A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Individual Learning Budget 

We invest in your professional growth! As part of our commitment to continuous learning, we offer an annual learning budget to support your personal and career development through courses, certifications, workshops and more.

Hybrid Work 

We’ve adopted a hybrid workplace model where 2 days in the office are recommended but not enforced. It’s up to you and your team to decide on the exact days you’ll spend working together in person.

Equal Opportunity 

The Vinted Group is committed to building an inclusive workplace where people from all walks of life feel a sense of belonging. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and life experiences. At Vinted, all applicants are treated fairly without regard to their race, age, religion or belief, sex, national origin, citizenship, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

€108.600 — €147.000 EUR

title: Principal Data Scientist
description:
The Principal Data Scientist is the senior technical and scientific leader for AbbVie 's omnichannel engagement analytics, a data- and analytics-driven engagement optimization program spanning channel mix, content, field representative call planning, and orchestration. Operating within the APEX Enterprise Advanced Analytics and Innovation team, this role sets the multi-year science vision for personalized commercial engagement and is accountable for the technical strategy, methodology, and scientific rigor of the AI/ML and statistical solutions that power it. Reporting to the Associate Director, Data Science, the Principal is a thought partner to commercial and analytics leadership: shaping which problems are worth solving, forming and defending a point of view on how AI creates measurable business value, and partnering with product owners to turn that vision into scalable solutions. The role combines deep, hands-on expertise in applied machine learning, generative AI, causal inference, and experimentation with the consultative skill to align a complex stakeholder ecosystem around the right answer.

Key Responsibilities

- Define the Data Science vision: Own the multi-year Data Science vision and technical roadmap for omnichannel engagement analytics, anticipating where both the business and the field of AI are heading.

- Shape how AI creates business value: identify, size, and prioritize opportunities where AI can drive measurable commercial impact, build the business case, and influence senior leadership decisions on where to invest.

- Lead hands-on with Gen-AI: Personally use AI-assisted development and agentic tools to prototype, test hypotheses, and demonstrate value quickly; build LLM-backed systems using advanced RAG and context engineering, paired with rigorous scientific evaluation frameworks to scale highly reliable omnichannel recommendations.

- Lead the design of predictive and causal models: Develop next-best-action, recommendation, and sequential decision models that inform customer engagement and resource allocation using complex, multi-source data.

- Own measurement science: set the standard for measuring effectiveness, incrementality, and business impact using experimental and quasi-experimental methods, so that AI investments are evaluated rigorously.

- Partner with product owners to shape problems, not just fulfill requirements: co-define business outcomes, scope, and success metrics, and translate them into scalable technical solutions.

- Navigate a complex stakeholder ecosystem: build alignment across brand and marketing leaders, field sales and operations, Medical, Legal and Regulatory (MLR), Compliance, BTS, Digital Lab, and external vendors; reframe requests into well-posed problems and resolve competing priorities.

- Communicate with executive impact: translate complex methods and findings into clear recommendations and compelling narratives for executive and non-technical audiences.

- Productionize at scale: Partner with BTS, Digital Lab, engineering, and platform teams to deploy, monitor, and manage the lifecycle of AI/ML solutions.

- Raise the bar for scientific rigor: establish best practices in model development, code quality, reproducibility, peer review, and responsible AI across the data science community.

- Be a thought leader: stay at the forefront of research and practice in machine learning, generative AI, and causal inference; bring new ideas into the team; provoke rigorous analytical debate; and represent AbbVie 's point of view internally and in the broader analytics community.

Supervisory / Management Responsibilities

This role does not carry formal direct report responsibilities but is expected to act as a technical leader and mentor across the broader data science community, raising the bar on scientific rigor and hands-on AI practice. The Principal Data Scientist may lead technical workstreams with external analytics vendors and partners, including oversight of deliverable quality and methodology validation.

Key Competencies

- Scientific Engineering Depth: Deep expertise in machine learning, causal inference, and generative AI, combined with strong engineering discipline in reproducibility, deployment, and enterprise integration.

- AI Fluency and Bias to Action: Uses AI hands-on in daily work to prototype, analyze, and build; critically evaluates AI output; and turns ideas into working solutions quickly.

- Business Judgment and Problem-Framing: Translates ambiguous business challenges into well-scoped problems, connects technical choices to commercial value, and sets long-term technical direction while staying close to delivery.

- Stakeholder Navigation and Executive Influence: Reads organizational dynamics to build alignment across commercial, regulatory, and technology partners, earning trust as a thought partner to win support from senior leaders.

- Thought Leadership: Challenges conventional thinking and sparks meaningful analytical debate with peers and executives.

Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or another quantitative discipline required; Master’s or PhD in a quantitative field strongly preferred.

Required Experience

- 8+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, or applied science (or 6+ years with a PhD), with a track record of delivering production-quality models that drove measurable business impact.

- Demonstrated experience setting technical direction for a portfolio of AI/ML solutions and influencing decisions of senior business leaders.

- Experience building personalization, recommendation, decision-optimization, or marketing-science solutions, in any industry.

- Deep hands-on expertise in causal inference and experimentation, including A/B testing and quasi-experimental methods, to measure business impact.

- Demonstrated hands-on experience using generative AI and AI-assisted development tools (e.g., LLM APIs, AI coding assistants, agent frameworks) to prototype and deliver solutions, with concrete examples that can be walked through during the interview process.

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience in deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and distributed data processing.

- Experience productionizing AI/ML solutions in cloud environments, including deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management.

- Track record of leading initiatives across complex, cross-functional stakeholder environments and presenting to executive audiences.

Preferred Experience

- Commercial analytics experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare, or life sciences, including familiarity with data sources such as IQVIA, Symphony Health, APLD, or similar Rx, claims, and engagement data.

- Experience in omnichannel analytics, such as journey analysis, touchpoint measurement, closed-loop measurement, or next-best-action for HCP or patient engagement.

- Experience with advanced ML and optimization methods, including reinforcement learning, multi-armed bandits, transformers, and other approaches for sequential or recommendation use cases.

- Experience building LLM-based and agentic AI systems, including orchestration frameworks, evaluation, and integration through APIs and pipelines.

- Experience with cloud ML platforms and MLOps tools such as Azure ML, Databricks, and MLflow.

- External visibility through conference talks, publications, patents, open-source contributions, or recognized industry thought leadership.

- Experience working in agile product development environments.

title: Software Engineer, Product
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

You'll work across LabOS — our internal software platform — building the orchestration layer that coordinates everything from experiment scheduling to execution to data capture and results processing. This is full-stack product engineering at the intersection of software and physical-world biology.

Day-to-day, that can mean things like:

- Creating interfaces and APIs that give scientists and AI agents visibility into what's happening in the lab in real time

- Building custom AI agents and tooling that automate decisions across the experiment lifecycle, from protocol design to troubleshooting failed results

- Turning proprietary hardware into API-controllable devices that agents and software can operate programmatically

- Designing scheduling systems that coordinate dozens of lab instruments with complex dependency chains

You'll own large areas of the product. We're a small team where individual engineers have large impact on what gets built and how.

What we're looking for 

- Full-stack production experience. We use TypeScript, React, Node, Postgres — but what matters is you can work across the stack.

- Product instinct. You've shipped, watched users, iterated, and shipped again.

- Comfortable in ambiguity. You start from a goal, not a spec. You scope problems down, decide what to build and what to skip, and write your own plan when none exists.

- Builds with AI. You use AI tools heavily, but you have enough experience without them to know what good looks like.

- Curious about biology. No background required, but running real experiments in the physical world should excite you.

Application deadline 

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

title: (Senior) Backend Engineer C++ (All Genders)
description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments. 

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions. 

WHY JOIN US 

- The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty. 

- You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms. 

- We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing. 

About the Team 

Minerva is STARK's command and control software — the brain that connects operators to autonomous systems across multiple domains in real time. The Minerva team is a small, senior software group based in Berlin and Munich, working directly with our systems and hardware teams to build mission-critical C2 capabilities deployed in active operational environments. 
We move fast, ship real software, and operate under constraints most engineers never encounter — low-bandwidth networks, air-gapped devices, high-stakes decision loops. There is no room for abstraction for its own sake. Everything we build ends up in the hands of real operators in the field. 

Your Mission 

This is not a "standard" backend role. You won't be building CRUD apps for a web store. You will be building the high-performance, low-latency engine at the heart of Minerva Frontline, our Command & Control (C2) Software, enabling mission planning and operations of Aerial and Maritime asset swarms in real world conditions. 
We are looking for C++ developers to build out our core server-side architecture enabling the increasingly complex CONOPS required by NATO’s Armed forces. You will be responsible for how we maintain a global battlefield state, how we translate high-level operator intents into machine-executable actions, and how we stream real-time telemetry to the frontline. 
You will work in a high-density engineering environment alongside robotics, safety, and mission planning experts. If you care about RAII, memory safety, and squeezing every ounce of performance out of real hardware in the field to ensure mission success, this is the role.
What we build: 

- The System Brain: You will develop the core C++ services that orchestrate UAV and USV swarms, maintaining a synchronized and robust battlefield state across distributed systems. 

- Mission Control APIs: You will design and implement high-performance gRPC and REST APIs that bridge the gap between our frontend C2 interface and the autonomous vehicles in the field. 

- Real-Time Data Pipelines: You will build and optimize the telemetry pipelines that handle high-frequency data from diverse sensors, ensuring low-latency synchronization and delivery. 

- Scalable Architecture: You will expand our current C++ architecture to support "affordable mass"—scaling from controlling 4 to 20+ vehicles simultaneously. 

- Tactical Integration: You will implement military standards and protocols (such as STANAG), ensuring our systems are interoperable and battle-ready. 

- Robustness & Testing: You will build and maintain the test suites, ensuring our code performs reliably under the most contested conditions. 

Responsibilities 

- A C++ Native: You write clean, performant Modern C++ (17/20/23). You understand the cost of every allocation and the value of a deterministic system. 

- Systems-Minded: You think in terms of data flows, state machines, and concurrency. You understand that in our domain, "late data is wrong data." 

- A Problem Solver: You dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems at the hardware-software boundary. 

- High Agency: You don't wait for perfect specifications. You understand the mission, look at the code, and drive the architecture forward. 

- Collaborative: You thrive in a multidisciplinary team, working closely with frontend, robotics, and integration engineers to deliver a cohesive product. 

Required Skills 

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in backend or systems engineering, with a primary focus on high-performance C++ applications. 

- C++ Expertise: Deep proficiency in Modern C++ (17 or later). 

- Networking: Strong understanding of asynchronous networking, inter-process communication (IPC), and real-time data streaming. 

- Industry Context: Relevant experience in Aerospace, Robotics, Automotive, Sensors, or High-Frequency Trading—any domain where software interacts with the physical world in real-time. 

- Bonus Skills: Familiarity with autopilot/flight control systems (MAVLink/PX4/ArduPilot), geospatial data handling (GIS), or building safety-critical software systems. 

If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, and you see yourself reflected on the description above, please send us your CV in English . We're looking forward to meeting you! 

SECURITY CLEARANCE 

Due to the nature of our work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate security clearance required for this position. Details will be provided during the recruitment process. 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 

We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Senior Data Scientist, AD/ADAS
description:
Woven by Toyota is enabling Toyota’s once-in-a-century transformation into a mobility company. Inspired by a legacy of innovating for the benefit of others, our mission is to challenge the current state of mobility through human-centric innovation — expanding what “mobility” means and how it serves society.

Our work centers on four pillars: AD/ADAS, our autonomous driving and advanced driver assist technologies; Arene, our software development platform for software-defined vehicles; Woven City, a test course for mobility; and Cloud & AI, the digital infrastructure powering our collaborative foundation. Business-critical functions empower these teams to execute, and together, we’re working toward one bold goal: a world with zero accidents and enhanced well-being for all.

TEAM 

At Woven by Toyota, we tackle Autonomy challenges at the intersection of AI, Robotics, and Advanced Driving. We develop advanced Perception and Planning technologies, and their production software for multiple AD/ADAS systems. To deliver reliable data-driven technologies to millions of Toyota vehicles, we are solving complex real-world problems using large-scale data, machine learning, and state-of-the-art architectures for Perception, Prediction, and Motion Planning.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

The team is looking for a strong Data Scientist to drive the creation and deployment of sophisticated data models and algorithms to resolve business challenges for the Autonomy team. You will combine modern data approaches with safety standards while also considering cost efficient options. You will be an expert in deep learning and software engineering. Furthermore, you are proactive towards handling the processes required for production development and approach them by asking "What can I do for you?" with a "Giver" mindset.

RESPONSIBILITIES 

- 
Develop data strategies on how to collect, sample, label, handle, and leverage large amounts of data from Toyota’s market fleet, test vehicles, and simulators, to directly improve machine learning model performance across perception and planning stacks

- 
Lead data-related activities across the autonomy team (perception, planning, product evaluation, etc), and across the company in collaboration with the Toyota group, by collaborating closely with stakeholders from multiple teams in different time-zones

- 
Analyze large-scale data and identify its characteristics to propose technical solutions for data curation, model improvement and performance evaluation techniques

- 
Develop evaluation frameworks and metrics to assess planner performance, identifying edge cases and high-value scenarios to improve system behavior.

- 
Design and improve the scalable data pipelines and automation for machine learning and performance evaluation

- 
Enhance the overall team capabilities in data science by initiating and leading initiatives across the Autonomy teams and mentor team members.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 

- 
Masters or PhD degree in a quantitative field related to Science and Engineering.

- 
5+ years experience in following industries or research areas: AD/ADAS, Robotics, Computer Vision, or Behavioral Planning.

- 
3+ years experience in data science or related areas, including theoretical aspects of data science like machine learning (deep learning, statistical analysis, A/B testing, and mathematical modeling)

- 
Experience in building machine learning algorithms and infrastructure, such as: data pre- and post-processing, sampling and curation, ablation studies, evaluation

title: Engineering Lead – AI Enablement (m/f/d)
description:
Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market.

Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns.

Team 

AI Enablement builds Raisin's internal AI platform. We make it easy and safe for every team, from engineering and product to business operations, to use AI in their daily work and in the products they build.

We provide the shared foundation for that: governed access to AI models and tools, the controls that keep data secure and usage auditable, and the visibility teams need to run AI reliably and cost-effectively. We also shape how Raisin builds software with AI, from AI-assisted coding to agentic workflows that support teams across the development lifecycle. Because Raisin operates in regulated financial services, security and compliance are core to how we design the platform.

The team is growing, and you will shape both what it builds and how it works.

Your Responsibilities 

As Engineering Lead, you lead the engineers who build Raisin's internal AI platform and drive the company's AI-assisted engineering practices. You are accountable for the team's delivery, growth, and maintaining the AI platform users' trust. 

You stay close to the technology, because in a field that changes this quickly, good leadership decisions depend on understanding the technical details.

Lead and grow the team 

- Hire, onboard, and develop engineers, and build a team that works autonomously across platform engineering, infrastructure, and AI.

- Hold regular 1:1s, set clear expectations, and agree individual development plans with each engineer.

- Give timely feedback, recognise strong performance, and address low performance early.

- Create an environment of trust, open communication, and continuous learning, so the team keeps up with a fast-moving field without burning out.

Own delivery and operations 

- Own end-to-end delivery, from planning and estimation through implementation and release, balancing new capabilities with reliability and maintenance.

- Make sure the platform runs well in production: on-call, incident handling, and service levels for the systems other teams rely on.

- Spot risks and blockers early and resolve them, or escalate in time with a clear proposal.

- Turn the AI strategy into quarterly goals and a roadmap the team commits to, together with your manager and stakeholders.

Run the platform as a product 

- Work with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to understand their needs and decide what the platform should offer next.

- Measure adoption, reliability, cost, and impact, and use that data in planning and when reporting to leadership.

- Manage the cost of AI usage and tooling, including budgets, licences, vendor relationships, and build-versus-buy decisions.

Shape the technical direction 

- Work with the team's tech leads on architecture and key technical decisions, and stay hands-on in design discussions, reviews, and selected implementation work.

- Work with security, legal, and compliance colleagues to keep the platform and the company's use of AI secure and compliant.

- Help engineering teams across Raisin adopt AI in their work through documentation, workshops, and direct support.

Your Profile 

What you bring 

- 3+ years leading engineers as an Engineering Manager, Engineering Lead, or Team Lead, including hiring and performance management.

- 7+ years in software engineering overall, with a background in backend, platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling.

- Experience leading a team that builds for internal customers, such as a platform, developer tooling, or shared services used by other engineers.

- A track record of delivering production systems that other teams depend on, including ownership of their reliability.

- A practical understanding of modern AI integration, such as LLM APIs, AI coding assistants, and agentic workflows, deep enough to evaluate technical decisions and challenge the team. You use AI tools in your own work.

- Clear communication with engineers, product, and business stakeholders, and fluency in English.

Nice to have 

- Experience with AI platform topics such as model access, governance, observability, rate limiting, or cost management.

- You have driven adoption of new tools or practices across an engineering organisation.

- Experience leading distributed or hybrid teams.

- Experience in a regulated industry such as banking or fintech.

You don't need to tick every box. If you have led a platform or developer-tooling team and you are excited about what AI changes for engineering, we would like to hear from you.

Join our mission, join our team – and grow with us! 

At Raisin, we care about each other and it is one of our top priorities to foster an open and caring environment in which everyone feels welcome and comfortable. Our culture is strongly driven by our ambitious team, which connects more than 75 different nationalities.

As part of our team, you will benefit from:

title: Software Engineer, Lab Automation
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

- Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

- Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

- Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

- Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

- Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

- Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

- Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

- Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

- Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

- Lab automation experience is a strong plus. Familiarity with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling helps — as does a background in robotics, industrial automation, IoT, or embedded systems.

- Maker and hacker attitude. You like figuring out how closed systems work and building the thing that makes them work better. Bonus if you're comfortable with electronics, microcontrollers, or a 3D printer when an integration needs a physical fix.

- AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

- Self-starter and independent. You define what needs building from how the lab actually works, not just what's in the ticket.

- Reliability-minded. The lab runs 24/7; you design systems where one instrument failing doesn't cascade through the whole work cell.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the code runs real experiments.

Details

- Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site — you need hands-on access to physical instruments).

- Type: Full time

- Start date: ASAP

Application deadline 

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

title: Graduate, Manufacturing Operations (Product Test) 2027
description:

Applications deadline : Midnight, 29th November 2026

The Graduate Programme at Graphcore

Join Graphcore in a permanent role and start your career with two years of hands-on learning. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, share your ideas and help shape what we’re creating. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are.

What you’ll work on 

Put your engineering knowledge to work on how advanced AI hardware moves from design into manufacture. 

As a Manufacturing Operations Graduate across Product Test, you’ll rotate through teams that turn complex AI technology into reliable products. You’ll support silicon package assembly, printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) production, component selection and bill of materials (BoM) management. 

You’ll analyse manufacturing and product performance data, investigate issues and help shape tests that support better engineering decisions. Your work will help Graphcore deliver high-quality hardware through global manufacturing partners, including production activity in Taiwan. 

Your team and support 

The Manufacturing Operations group brings together Manufacturing Technology & Process, Product Test, Quality, and Logistics and Procurement. You’ll be based in Bristol, working with colleagues across the UK, Taiwan and India. 

You’ll learn from experienced people through practical problem solving with engineering teams, operations specialists and external manufacturing partners. Decisions are guided by data, with input from design, test, quality and delivery specialists. 

You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and share ideas for making things better. Gather evidence, take responsibility for your work and speak up when you spot a problem or need support. 

How you’ll learn and grow 

During the two-year programme, rotations will help you build broad foundations across manufacturing, quality, product test and supply chain. 

Hands-on work will show you how engineering decisions affect product quality and delivery. You’ll learn to connect manufacturing data with product performance, investigate problems and use tests to compare approaches and guide improvements. 

Working with specialists across the group will help you understand how each part of the manufacturing process fits together. You’ll build your technical judgement and communication skills as you explain findings and contribute to decisions, with experienced colleagues around you to support your development. 

What we're looking for 

- Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics or a related technical field 

- Curiosity about semiconductor manufacturing, PCBA production or server hardware 

- Comfort using data to investigate problems, explain findings and support decisions, with a practical approach to testing, learning and improving your work 

- Exposure to Python, Linux, Bash, Git or similar engineering tools 

- Bring clear communication, willingness to take ownership of your work and openness to sharing your observations when something needs attention  

You can demonstrate these skills through coursework, a dissertation, personal or team projects, research, or other relevant experience. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned. 

Benefits

- Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility

- Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension

- Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success

- Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day

- Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones

- Electric Vehicle Scheme: Choose an electric vehicle and lease it through salary sacrifice

- Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover

- Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn

We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.

Sponsorship

Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.

Introduction to Graphcore

At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: from semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.

How to apply and what to expect 

To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.

Ready to put your learning into practice? Start your manufacturing operations career across Product Test in a permanent role, with two years of hands-on learning through the Graphcore Graduate Programme. Apply now and help shape what comes next.
