title: Product Owner
description:
Functieomschrijving 

Als Product Owner Interne Automatisering & IT ben jij de onmisbare brug tussen de business en ons IT-landschap. Je haalt de wensen en requirements op bij verschillende afdelingen en het Management Team, en vertaalt deze naar slimme, efficiënte automatiseringen. Waar anderen een complex proces zien, zie jij een kans om zaken sneller, beter en soepeler te laten verlopen. 

In deze rol schakel je veel met interne stakeholders om processen echt te doorgronden. Vervolgens bepaal je hoe we onze tools, waaronder ons ERP-systeem Odoo en Camunda, optimaal kunnen inzetten. Je werkt hierbij nauw samen met onze Applicatiebeheerder, die het functionele beheer voor zijn rekening neemt en onze Camunda/Python Developer. Omdat onze developer ook eigen projecten draait, is het fantastisch als jij zelf de taal van developers spreekt of zelfs je eigen Python-code kunt kloppen om snel iets te bouwen of testen. 

Taken en verantwoordelijkheden 

- Ophalen, analyseren en in kaart brengen van requirements bij diverse afdelingen en de MT-laag. 

- Vertalen van bedrijfsprocessen en wensen naar concrete automatiseringsoplossingen. 

- Beheren, prioriteren en structureren van de interne IT-backlog. 

- Samenwerken met de interne Camunda/Python developer en de Applicatiebeheerder om projecten succesvol en vlot op te leveren. 

- Adviseren van de business over procesoptimalisaties en nieuwe automatiseringskansen. 

- Zorgdragen voor een soepele implementatie en adoptie van nieuwe functionaliteiten op de werkvloer. 

Over Payter 

Bij Payter zijn we pioniers op het gebied van contactloze NFC- en cashless-technologie. Sinds 2007 maken we impact: we hebben het grootste Europese proefproject voor contactloze en mobiele betalingen gelanceerd, en sindsdien maken bedrijven over de hele wereld gebruik van onze oplossingen. We combineren innovatieve technologieën om veilige, duurzame en toekomstbestendige producten te ontwikkelen. Bij Payter krijg je de kans om bij te dragen aan slimme oplossingen die écht verschil maken in een snel veranderende wereld. 

- Je hebt hbo-werk- en -denkniveau en een sterke interesse in IT en bedrijfsprocessen. 

- Je bent communicatief vaardig, stapt makkelijk op mensen af en kunt goed schakelen met zowel de business als technische collega's. 

- Je snapt hoe bedrijfsprocessen lopen en wordt oprecht enthousiast van het automatiseren hiervan. 

- Je hebt (basis)kennis van Python; het is een hele mooie bonus als je zelf ook af en toe wat code kunt schrijven. 

- Je hebt bij voorkeur kennis van of interesse in ERP-systemen (zoals Odoo) 

- Je bent analytisch, nieuwsgierig en pakt graag de regie om projecten van wens tot realiteit te brengen. 

- Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. 

Wat Wij Bieden 

- Ruimte voor professionele ontwikkeling met trainingen en andere ontwikkelmogelijkheden 

- 25 vakantiedagen 

- 12 balancedays voor een goede werk-privébalans 

- Gratis lunch op het kantoor 

- Werken in een dynamische en energieke omgeving 

- Meegroeien met Payter en echt impact maken 

- Goed bereikbaar kantoor

title: Principal MEMS Development Engineer
description:
About SiTime 

SiTime Corporation is the precision timing company. Our semiconductor MEMS programmable solutions offer a rich feature set that enables customers to differentiate their products with higher performance, smaller size, lower power and better reliability. With more than 3 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit www.sitime.com .

Job Summary 

Join the team that is revolutionizing the timing industry with the best silicon Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) timing products in the world. As a Principal MEMS Development Engineer, you will use your technical and creative problem-solving skills to push forward MEMS technology and engineer resonators for SiTime’s next-generation timing products. It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position.

Responsibilities: 

- Lead definition and execution of challenging technical projects. 

- Advise management of challenges, impact, recommendations.

- Develop new or improved resonators, MEMS technologies and/or products.

- Design MEMS devices and characterize their electrical, mechanical, and thermal performance on wafer level and/or device level. 

- Work with process team to drive continuous improvement in MEMS yields.

- Extend and enhance automated infrastructure for MEMS design, measurements, and data analysis.

- Design and analyze experiments to understand device physics, materials, and fabrication.

- Interface with local and overseas vendors.

- Work in cross-functional teams, including circuits, systems, and packaging.

- Working/supporting other projects as needed.

Qualifications & Requirements: 

- Ph.D. in ME, EE, Physics, or equivalent

- At least 3 years of industry experience.

- Skilled scientist with ability to design, conduct, and analyze experiments.

- Excellent problem identification and problem-solving abilities.

- Excellent knowledge of mechanics, electrodynamics, thermodynamics.

- Knowledge in fundamentals of MEMS devices physics and fabrication.

- Experience with finite element simulation tools (COMSOL, ANSYS) and data processing tools (Matlab, Python).

- Excellent interpersonal, organizational, written and verbal communication skills.

- Passion for delivering exceptional results.

Desired Characteristics & Attributes: 

- 3 -10 years of industry experience.

- Intermediate to advanced knowledge of programing languages, circuits, metrology equipment and methods.

- Experience with Statistical analysis and tools such as R or JMP.

- Knowledge in MEMS microfabrication.

Compensation Range: 

At SiTime, we believe great work deserves great rewards. We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive compensation package designed to attract top talent. 

In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for a quarterly bonus tied to the achievement of innovation goals—reflecting our commitment to recognizing meaningful impact. We also offer equity grants, providing a meaningful opportunity to share in the company’s future growth and success.

SiTime is an Equal Opportunity Employer . We treat each person fairly and we do not tolerate discrimination or harassment against anyone on the basis of any protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, pregnancy, political affiliation, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, or marital status or other characteristics protected by law.

description:
Ditto | Engineering & Product | Remote (US: Atlanta, Austin, SF, Seattle) + APAC | Full-time
https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/ditto https://docs.ditto.live/home/about-ditto I've been obsessed with CRDTs since I first saw them at Strange Loop years ago, and I still can't quite believe I now get to work on them for a living — in some of the most challenging environments there are: disconnected, degraded, contested, out where the cloud isn't. If that's your kind of problem, come build with us. Ditto is the edge-native data platform that keeps distributed systems in sync when the network doesn't cooperate — an offline-first, CRDT-based layer syncing any device (phone, vehicle, sensor, server) over Bluetooth LE, P2P Wi-Fi, LAN, and tactical radio, with or without connectivity. Same core, commercial to defense; operationally deployed and network-agnostic. The problems are the fun kind: conflict-free replication with no server and no synchronized clock, multi-transport routing that never drops the connection, moving a coherent picture over links as thin as an HF radio shot, and human-in-the-loop robotics/autonomy where a detection may have to be physically carried by a moving node. Concept to field in days, not months. Most roles are open to anyone authorized to work in the U.S.; Public Sector and forward-deployed roles require U.S. person status. Remote in the U.S. (hubs: Atlanta, Austin, SF, Seattle) unless noted. Product — Senior PM: Cloud Database & Integrations; Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Engineering — Engineering Manager, Data Sync Public Sector (U.S. persons) — Senior SWE: Autonomy · Systems FDE · Portal (ATL/remote) · FDE (SF, on-site); SWE, Public Sector Application Core Technologies — Senior SWE: Rust · Data Sync · Database · Networking · Bluetooth · React Native SDK · Android (ATL) Cloud Services — Senior SWE, Cloud (x2) Infrastructure — Staff SWE, Platform; Senior Platform Engineer, Operator; Senior SRE; Senior SRE, APAC (remote) If interested apply above and mention Hackernews.July.26

description:
Loft Orbital | Senior Cloud Infrastructure Engineer (SRE) | Golden, CO or San Francisco, CA | $180k–$240k + equity | https://loftorbital.com Loft builds and operates shareable satellites so customers can fly a payload without building a spacecraft. We integrate, launch, and operate the mission end to end: Earth observation, IoT, on-orbit AI, national security. 30+ missions flown since 2017, fleet on track for 30 satellites by 2027, offices in SF, Golden, and Toulouse. Our Cloud Infrastructure team runs the ground segment that talks to the fleet. - Reliability: RCAs, fault tolerance, performance tuning, long-term fixes over patches
- Software-defined networking between ground stations, cloud, and mission ops
- Developer experience: tooling and environments for the flight software and ops teams Looking for: strong public cloud (ideally GCP), deep Kubernetes, one backend language (Go/Python/Rust/C++/Java), IaC + CI/CD in anger, and someone who can design HA systems and then run them. Nice to have: FinOps, security tooling, orchestration in resource-constrained environments. Benefits: 100% company-paid medical/dental/vision for you and dependents, 401(k) + equity, flexible PTO + 12 holidays, 14/10 weeks paid parental leave, daily catered lunch, relocation assistance, and time with the team in France. Apply: https://jobs.lever.co/loftorbital/3ae5c3e3-c1e0-4311-83b5-0b... and mention HN in your application.

title: Head of Finance
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We are building the most automated lab in the world, and that does not stop at the bench. A company that AI agents can run experiments in has to automate everything around the experiment too — procurement, hiring, admin, and finance. Finance is one of the most automatable functions in any company and almost nobody has actually done it. We intend to.

That is the job: build an AI-powered finance stack. Our ledger, billing, cards and payroll all expose APIs, and we already close the books against them programmatically rather than by hand. You would take that much further, to where the model, the close, the cash view and the margin analysis largely run themselves, and your week goes on the decisions instead of the reconciliation.

You would be our first finance hire, and it is hands-on. You will build the forecast, run the close across two entities, own cash, and be the person who can say what a protein actually costs us to make.

What You'll Do

- Own the forecast. Both directions: bottom-up from lab capacity, throughput and price per protein, and top-down P&L, burn and runway.

- Own gross margin. What does an experiment actually cost us — DNA, reagents, consumables, instrument time, labour? Which products and which customers lose us money?

- Own pricing, with commercial. What we charge, why, and where the floor is. Pricing at a lab company is a finance question wearing a sales hat.

- Own the close. Group consolidation and intercompany management. Make it fast, make it correct, make it boring.

- Own cash. Bank and card accounts across Switzerland and the US, AP runs, AR collection, payment timing. Know where the money is and where it is going before anyone asks.

- Keep us compliant. Tax, VAT, audit, payroll, and the external firms we work with. You are not a lawyer or an accountant, but you know when to call one.

- Investor reporting, fundraising support, and treasury management. 

- Equipment leasing and asset management. The lab runs on millions of francs of instruments. Lease or buy, how we finance it, what it does to the balance sheet, and keeping the asset register honest as we expand.

- Automate all of the above. 

What We're Looking For

- You have built a finance function, not just worked in one. Several years in finance at a startup that actually scaled, and ideally you were early enough to have set things up rather than inherited them.

- You can build a real model. Not a template. A model that ties operational reality — throughput, yield, capacity, headcount — to cash, and that survives someone pulling on it.

- You write code, or you are visibly about to. SQL at minimum, Python ideally. This is the hard requirement most finance candidates will fail, and we mean it. We run on Claude Code across the company, and every system finance touches has an API behind it. The best version of this person automates their own function, writes their own tooling, and finds leverage the rest of us have not thought of. If your instinct is that finance is a spreadsheet-and-portal job, we will frustrate each other.

- You understand the cost structure of a physical business. Reagents, instruments, consumables, capex versus COGS, yield loss. Lab, hardware, or manufacturing backgrounds all translate. Pure SaaS finance does not, on its own.

- Swiss and European finance experience. VAT, social charges, employment law. A US entity alongside a Swiss one is a plus.

- Ambitious, and in it for the company. We want someone who intends to be running finance at a much larger Adaptyv in three years, and who cares about what we are building rather than the title on the door.

- Trustworthy with everything. Salaries, revenue, investor communications, board material. All of it crosses your desk.

Scope

We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a room with a customer, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing.

The centre of gravity is the numbers: the model, the close, cash, margin, pricing, and the board pack. That is the part that is yours and the part we will judge the role on. Procurement is a separate hire and the two of you will be joined at the hip on cost, but the sourcing and the vendor relationships are not yours to run.

One thing it is not: a bookkeeping seat. The mechanical layer is handled, and if that is the job you want, this one will bore you.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most first-finance-hires at a startup spend three years cleaning up a SaaS P&L. Here, the finance question and the product question are the same question: an automated lab is a machine for converting money into experimental data, and how efficiently it does that is literally the business. You will be building the model of that machine, at a company that is about to expand it several-fold, while it is being used by the best pharma companies and the best AI labs in the world. And you will do it with a founding team that will hand you the API keys and get out of your way.

JustPark | Senior Software Engineer, Reporting | Hybrid: Dallas, TX | Full-Time/Perm | Competitive salary + Benefits. Apply at: https://apply.workable.com/j/FE43DE896A JustPark is the premier partner offering both B2B solutions for destinations and B2C services for drivers, giving us the best of both worlds. We simplify the entire parking experience. From venues and councils to private driveways, our platform makes it simple for drivers to find, book, and pay for parking—while empowering our operating partners to deliver exceptional parking experiences. Join the JustPark Reporting team. You'll build, ship and maintain the data platform and reporting products behind our venue operations, used at venues like Mercedes Benz Stadium, The Greek Theatre and The O2 Arena. Following the 2024 merger of ParkHub and JustPark, we're scaling internationally, which means distributed systems, teams, and interesting problems at the intersection of payments, data and real time event operations. This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll own meaningful pieces of our platform from design through production, including keeping them healthy on live event days. 
We're an AI native engineering team: engineers use Claude Code, Copilot and Cursor as daily tools for code generation, review, debugging and documentation, and we build MCP integrations that connect our AI tools directly to Jira, Confluence, Slack and internal APIs so engineers stay in flow. 
You'll work closely with Product, QA, and our UK engineering and data teams to shape the data strategy of a fast growing international company. Some of what you'll be doing:
-Design, build and ship backend services and streaming data pipelines in Go that handle real world scale
-Own data end to end: event schema and contract design, durable messaging patterns, and the read models and warehouse tables analytics is served from
-Build financial data flows, including payment processor ingestion, fee reconciliation and ledger backed reporting
-Ingest and reconcile third party data (partner files and payment processor APIs) with idempotent, replayable backfills
-Develop and evolve API and GraphQL serving layers that power our internal and external products
-Migrate existing reporting paths onto the new architecture

description: Lumen Labs | Robotics / Hardware Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $130k–200k + equity | https://lumenresearch.co I'm Daniel, co-founder. Lumen Labs is building the cognitive layer for physical AI. Nearly every major robotics effort today teaches machines by showing them thousands of hours of human teleoperation. We think that paradigm has a ceiling, and we're working on nature-inspired architectures for unstructured environments (construction sites, mining, pipelines, battlefield). Pre-seed, backed by top VC funds and operators from robotics/AI companies. We're a team of two and hiring teammate #3 to own the hardware and infrastructure that keeps our research platforms running: the ROS2 (Humble) stack across onboard and offboard compute, sensor integration and calibration (LiDAR, depth, IMU, encoders), the safety pipeline during autonomous runs, and getting trained policies onto real hardware. Today that's wheeled navigation; we're dipping our toes into drones and eyeing weirder platforms like pipeline inspection. Where we're at: zero-shot sim2real transfer with a policy that runs at 100Hz on an ESP32 and took under a day to train. You: hands-on with real mobile robots (UART, encoders, PWM, IMU, LiDAR), strong Python + embedded, comfortable reading code you didn't write, and can debug hardware and firmware at the same time. If "full-stack" to you means firmware, a multimeter, and a ROS node in the same afternoon, you'll fit right in. Visa/relocation support for the right person. Full posting: https://desert-bearskin-26d.notion.site/Robotics-Engineer-Ro... Email hi@lumenresearch.co, mention HN, and tell us about a project you've built. If you can link to a time you got a trained policy running on real hardware, you go to the top of the pile.

title: MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time
description:
MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time
MixRank processes petabytes of data every month through web crawling. Hundreds of customers use our data products, including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries such as finance, recruiting, sales, marketing, and security. We’re a fully remote company with a global footprint across 20+ countries. We’re growing, profitable, employee-owned, and have no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome. We’re looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job, but something they genuinely love to do. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours through full automation and will be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in under two minutes.Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git. We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We run two datacenters with high-performance servers we’ve built ourselves, capable of handling the volumes of data we process. We’ve implemented our own distributed file system, perform full-scale web crawls, and download and run static analysis on the entire universe of published Android APKs and iOS IPAs. Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that help you grow as an individual. We’re continuously hiring for the positions below; these aren’t singular roles that close once filled. Our philosophy is that the candidate is more important than the position. For each new member of the team, we design a custom role and responsibilities around their interests.
Other companies may create a long list of specific requirements with the expectation that you’ll exactly replace someone on the team or fit a role defined by committee. MixRank is more pragmatic: we first get excited about bringing a unique individual onto the team, then figure out the best way to support their specific talents. Junior Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re looking for remote junior engineers with 0–3 years of professional software experience and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects. This is an open-ended entry role with mentorship and diverse opportunities to work across all areas of our product: databases, distributed systems, infrastructure and tooling, data analysis, machine learning, frontend/backend web development, APIs, data mining, data modeling, and more. To stand out, please highlight what makes you unique: passion for computing, curiosity and side projects, work ethic, niche research, or anything else that shows how you think and build. Ideally, you’ve already graduated. But if you still have one or more years left of school, please feel free to apply anyway. If you’re the right fit for the team, we’ll figure out a way to accommodate your schedule. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/Fnwsojk-j Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re hiring generalist software engineers to work on web applications, data mining, machine learning/data science, data transformation/ETL, data modeling, database scaling, infrastructure, DevOps, and more. We’ll tailor the role to the subset of areas that best match your interests. Beneficial experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/RXQspen-s I’m Kiran, Chief of Staff at MixRank, a fully remote data startup building go-to-market intelligence. We’re US-incorporated but hire globally, and we’re bringing on new teammates to join a fast-moving team with real ownership and impact.

Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

About the Role 

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it.

- Contribute to front-end and admin workflows where needed: The role is primarily backend-focused, but you'll contribute to internal-facing UI and ops tooling where the product requires it.

description: Prior Labs | Berlin, Freiburg, NYC | ONSITE | Full-time | Technical PM, ML Infra, Research Scientist/Engineer, Backend, Full Stack We build foundation models for tabular data. Deep learning transformed text and images but mostly skipped tables, which are still the data behind most clinical trials, financial models and scientific experiments. The reason is structural: no natural sequence, no spatial structure, no shared vocabulary across datasets, so the architectures and scaling laws behind LLMs don't transfer. Our approach: pre-train a transformer on millions of synthetic datasets sampled from causal-structure priors. The whole dataset goes in as context, predictions come out in one forward pass. No per-dataset training, no hyperparameter tuning, seconds instead of hours. TabPFN v2 was published in Nature and set a new state of the art; TabPFN-3 scales to 10M rows. 4M+ downloads, 8k+ GitHub stars, in production from liquid biopsy to rail maintenance. Code: https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN Since July we're an independent lab inside SAP, with more than EUR 1B committed over four years. Models stay open, research stays public, same team and offices. Roles (most can sit in any of the three offices): - Technical Product Manager, Integrations: take every model release live across SAP (AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud), the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, and help decide which channels we build next. Reports to me, close to the code. - ML Engineer, Infrastructure: own multi-cluster GPU infra (Slurm on GCP today, multi-provider next), training performance and the tooling layer. We spend tens of millions per year on compute; you own that budget. - Research Scientist, Foundation Model: drive the model agenda - novel architectures, scaling from 10K to 1M+ samples, multimodal and causal directions. PhD plus top-venue publications, or equivalent. - Research Engineer, Foundation Model: same agenda from the engineering side. You design experiments, write the training and eval infra, and co-author the papers. - ML Engineer, Backend: design and scale the backend that serves and finetunes the models. Python/FastAPI, Terraform, K8s. - Full Stack Engineer, ML Platform: build the product end to end. TypeScript + Python, React/FastAPI/Postgres. Also hiring: Applied Scientist, Forward Deployed ML Engineer, Research Scientist (Foundational Data Science), PhD research interns, plus GTM and ops roles. 40+ people with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Jane Street, Goldman, G-Research, CERN. Led by Frank Hutter, advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Yann LeCun. Comp competitive with top AI labs. All roles and applications: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/prior-labs Questions welcome in the replies here.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Agents
description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The Role 

RevenueCat helps app developers manage subscriptions and make more money from them. Maybe you're an indie developer who doesn’t know what "conversion" even means, you just want your app to make money so you can keep building it. Or maybe you're a growth specialist at a company doing millions a month, and pricing experiments are already your whole job. Either way, you probably didn't get into this to spend your days staring at a dashboard. So we built two AI agents to do that work for you, or make you even sharper at it if you're already a pro.

Enter Rico. Rico watches over your subscription business and can help you make sense of it, and act on what it finds. Say your revenue dropped last week. You don't need to go digging through charts to find out why. Just ask Rico. It pulls the data, explains what happened in plain language, and shows you how you compare to similar apps. Then it can fix things itself, like setting up a new plan or restoring a customer's access, with you approving the change before it goes live. Run a pricing experiment and Rico will read the results for you and tell you which version is winning. There are so many things we want Rico to be able to do!

Then there's our AI Paywall Editor, a specialized agent to build and edit paywalls, the screen that asks someone to subscribe. Most developers are not designers, and a paywall that actually gets people to tap "subscribe" is harder to build than it looks, so the AI Paywall Editor helps you with that. Use it in our online editor, from the command line, or hook your own AI tools into it over MCP.

You can see both agents in action in our most recent product launch recap .

This is a role for engineers who've built advanced agents that do actual work , not just a thin wrapper around an LLM. You'll ship agentic features to thousands of developers, and you’ll shape the foundation everything else runs on: orchestration, tool execution, context management, evaluation and human-in-the-loop controls.

About You 

- 
You have 8+ years of experience shipping production systems.

- 
You've built agents that other people actually use and the systems around them: tool use, structured output, context management, evaluation, orchestration.

- 
You have strong backend fundamentals. You've built systems that need to be reliable, observable, and secure.

- 
You hold a high bar for quality and instinctively know which details matter, but also are discerning enough to cut scope when needed while still delivering value.

- 
You’re customer-obsessed: you imagine yourself as the developer, product manager, or marketer using the feature or experiencing the issue.

- 
You’re a builder, not an implementer: scoping, prioritizing, and driving rollout in partnership with our Product team. This isn’t a role where you check off items from a detailed specification.

- 
You can quickly familiarize yourself with code you didn't write yourself and improve it.

- 
You’re scrappy and biased toward shipping. You’d rather ship a good version today and iterate than wait to ship a perfect one next quarter.

- 
You communicate clearly, both in real-time and asynchronously. We’re a fully remote team, and how you write is as important as how you code.

- 
You’ve shipped meaningful user-facing features to production, monitored their usage and adoption, and improved them over time.

- 
You write high-quality, well-tested code, debug issues methodically, and help raise the engineering bar through thoughtful feedback and mentorship.

- 
You act like an founder:: you notice problems, propose improvements, and follow through fast.

- 
You're comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early stage product inside a growth stage company, and the architecture is still being figured out.

- 
You're self directed. You figure out what needs to be built, build it, and ship it.

- 
You are curious and stay current on AI tools and practices.

- 
You have a habit of sharing what you learn with others.

Ideally, you have: 

- 
Familiarity with subscription business models, app stores, or developer tools

- 
Experience with OpenAI/Anthropic APIs specifically

- 
Experience with observability frameworks (Langfuse, Langchain, etc.)

- 
Built Slack integrations

- 
Contributed to open source AI/ML tooling

- 
Maintained systems at scale

In the first month, you’ll: 

- 
Meet frequently with your team and manager to get up to speed

- 
Learn our tools, processes, and the subscription business concepts that shape our product

- 
Get familiar with our debugging tools, infrastructure, and overall architecture

- 
Ship your first project: a small feature that gets you into the codebase and shows you how the agents talk to RevenueCat's APIs

- 
Jump in early: fix bugs, ship small improvements, and weigh in on PRs

Within the first 3 months, you’ll: 

- 
Ship a medium sized project, ideally a new agentic feature that reaches tens of thousands of developers

- 
Understand the main product areas your team owns and how they work end to end

- 
Understand our current agent infrastructure, orchestration, the eval pipeline, the tool framework, and the trust and permissions layer, and have opinions on how to improve it

- 
Scope and work on projects on your own, from idea to post launch improvements

- 
Take part in code reviews, bug bashes, and technical discussions

Within the first 6 months, you’ll: 

- 
Become the go to engineer for certain focus areas

- 
Have made the agents measurably more reliable, faster, and capable

- 
Contribute to architecture discussions that affect more than just your team

- 
Mentor other engineers joining the team

- 
Talk directly with customers to understand how your work actually lands

- 
Debug issues across frontend, backend, and data. Communicate clearly during incidents and drive fixes that prevent repeats

- 
Learn the basics of incident response and join the on call rotation

Within the first 12 months, you’ll: 

- 
Have built infrastructure the rest of the team ships agents on top of

- 
Know all the major components of our system and be able to debug complex issues

- 
Write proposals and drive major architecture discussions

- 
Spec and architect large projects, gather feedback, and drive design validation and rollout plans

- 
Have made RevenueCat an AI native company in large part because you built the engine underneath it

- 
Have your own initiatives for improving our product and systems, grounded in real customer priorities

What we offer: 

- 
Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

- 
10-year window to exercise vested equity options

- 
A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

- 
4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

- 
Paid desk at a co-working space

- 
Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend

Interviewing at RevenueCat 

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat , including tips to help you succeed.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote

URL: https://www.samsara.com/ 

About the role: 

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We're still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we're hiring the engineers who will build what comes next.

We're approaching ~$2B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.

We're looking for software engineers who want to define what ships next. Leveling is broad and flexible: we're hiring from Senior through Staff+, across platform and product, and we're open to shaping scope around the right person's strengths and interests. That window won't stay open long.

This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role. 

You should apply if: 

- You want to impact the industries that run our world. The software you build will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn't metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.

- You want to build, not maintain. Samsara is in full growth mode. We're building new systems from scratch, not babysitting old ones. You'd own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.

- You want to work where AI meets the physical world. Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.

- You believe customers are more than a number. Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You'll participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.

- You have the curiosity and drive to figure it out. We're looking for people who take pride in their work and get things done at all costs. The engineers who thrive here don't wait to be told what to build. They define it, ship it, and own the outcome. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn't tooling or process. It's ambition.

In this role, you will: 

- Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.

- Define and drive technical strategy for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.

- Design and ship full-stack features end to end. You'll work across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile to deliver AI-powered products that solve real operational problems.

- Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes.

- Build and scale the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators.

- Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code reviews, design reviews, technical mentorship, and by setting a standard for quality, velocity, and craft.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role: 

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

- 8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.

- Strong full-stack fundamentals. You're comfortable working across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile) to ship complete products.

- Proficiency in modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).

- Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.

- Experience building AI-powered or data-driven products. You don't need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- A track record of building: zero-to-one products, systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.

An ideal candidate also has: 

- Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that's LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.

- Comfort with modern AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply your output and accelerate delivery.

- Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.

- A proven track record of mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.

- Side projects, open-source contributions, or other signals of curiosity and drive outside the scope of your day job.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary

$162,400 — $290,000 USD

Total Rewards 

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara 

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-staff-software-engineer

Build a Safer World.
